They cannot linger on that very long, though, because they play the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night. The vibes were so high and the Panthers were favored at home before dropping the egg of all eggs against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Now, a loss puts them below .500, souring what had been a really fun start to the season. Will they lose? Here's what the early odds say for this primetime bout. The Panthers are +160 to win outright, and the Packers are -192 on the moneyline. The oddsmakers don't have a lot of faith in the Panthers, despite both teams coming off a loss. So, unfortunately, there are plenty of reasons to expect the Panthers to lose, and it's unlikely they can replicate last season's magical upset. The same formula simply won't work, and the Packers will likely not underestimate them this time. Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Week 8 of the NFL season kicks off on Thursday night, as the Green Bay Packers and Jordan Love look to stay over .500 when they take on the Carolina Panthers and Bryce Young. Green Bay fell to 4-3 with a loss to Detroit in Week 7, and it's in last place in a loaded NFC North through seven weeks. Meanwhile, the Panthers (3-3) are in first place in the NFC South despite a major blowout loss at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Carolina made the playoffs in the 2025 season, but it has a ton of injuries on both sides of the ball that make it a tough team to trust against other quality opponents -- like Green Bay. Oddsmakers agree with that sentiment, as they've set the Packers as favorites at home to open this week. Panthers vs. Packers Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Panthers +3.5 (-110) Packers -3.5 (-110) Panthers: +154 Packers: -185 48.5 (Over -105/Under -115) There hasn't been a ton of movement in the odds for this game , as the Packers remain 3.5-point favorites at home. The total has jumped up from 47.5 to 48.5 while the moneyline has actually moved in Carolina's favor. According to DraftKings, just 22 percent of the moneyline bets and 41 percent of the spread bets are on the Panthers after their Week 7 showing against Tampa Bay. Earlier this week, I shared in SI Betting's preview for this game why I believe Green Bay is a worthwhile bet: The Panthers’ run defense was torched in Week 7 by Tampa Bay, and this could be a “get-right” spot for Matt LaFleur’s offense. Love should be able to attack through the air, as the Panthers are a below-average defense overall (20th in EPA/Play), and they entered Week 7 allowing the most yards per carry in the league. Meanwhile, Green Bay’s defense held a vaunted Detroit offense to just 20 points and is now fifth in the league in EPA/Play. If it weren’t for multiple missed field goals, the Pack could be entering this game with a 5-2 record. Carolina beat Detroit this season, but it has some confounding losses against Cleveland and at home against Tampa Bay. I don’t love this team – which is extremely banged up after Taylor Moton went down in Week 7 – on a short week against a Packers squad that has an above-average defense. I’m going to lay the points with a Green Bay team that needs this game a lot more than Carolina does if it’s going to make the playoffs. I'm not the only member of the SI Betting team taking Green Bay, as Iain MacMillan shared in his Road to 272 column -- where he bets on every NFL game, every week -- why he likes the Pack at home as well: I wrote about how I was out on the Panthers last week, and I proved to be right as they ended up on the wrong side of a blowout against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I'm still out on this Panthers team, as they seem like a significant regression candidate after a strong start to the season. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. There's always a chance these odds move further as the week goes on, so make sure to hang with the SI Betting team for the latest updates, player prop picks, final game predictions and more for Thursday Night Football in Week 8. That could lead to an expanded role for Irving, who was targeted 15 times out of the backfield in Mayfield's three starts this season. The veteran running back has been solid in the 2026 campaign, averaging 4.7 yards per carry across six games. Since then, Irving has just six total targets. Irving's presence is great news for a 1-5 Tampa Bay team that needs every win it can get to stay alive in the NFC South and the NFC playoff picture. However, they'll be without star receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) for the first time all season. Irving has 452 rushing yards, 74 receiving yards, two rushing scores and one receiving score this season. He'll look to build on that against a Carolina defense that has allowed the most yards per carry in the league in 2026. away.headline: Packers-Panthers Tuesday injury report: Time near for Micah Parsons, Kevin Zeitler?
away.blurb: The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted. Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers. There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit. Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay. Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle). Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers. The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard. More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening. There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice. “I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said. Will Kevin Zeitler Start at Right Guard? Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut? Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances. “If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.” Good News and Bad News for Packers Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. “I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”

The Carolina Panthers are looking to bounce back from a Week 7 loss as they share the field Thursday against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Green Bay. Carolina got some good news heading into that matchup, with wide receiver Jalen Coker practicing in full on Tuesday, according to the team’s latest injury report. away.headline: Bucs-Panthers Inactives | Baker Mayfield Returns to Action
away.blurb: After missing three games due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, quarterback Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday as they take on the Carolina Panthers in a critical intra-division game. Mayfield carried a questionable designation on the injury report into the weekend but was able to practice without limitations throughout the week. He intends to wear a specialized glove on his right hand that offers added support to the injured joint, preventing the thumb from being bent backward. Mayfield will not have the team's top receiving target at his disposal, however, as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out for Week Seven with both a concussion and a foot injury. In addition, starting right tackle Luke Goedeke is out due to a calf ailment and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will miss his third straight outing thanks to a rib fracture. The Buccaneers and Panthers submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Seven meeting at Bank of America Stadium. After elevating linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad, the Buccaneers had 54 available players and thus had to name six inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Panthers also elevated outside linebacker Nick Hampton and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad and had to name seven inactive players. Carolina will be without one of its top pass-rushers as Jaelan Phillips is out due to a hamstring strain. Fellow outside linebacker Thomas Incoom is also unavailable due to a calf issue, and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. home.headline: Packers-Panthers Tuesday injury report: Time near for Micah Parsons, Kevin Zeitler?
home.blurb: The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted. Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers. There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit. Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay. Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle). Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers. The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard. More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening. There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice. “I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said. Will Kevin Zeitler Start at Right Guard? Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut? Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances. “If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.” Good News and Bad News for Packers Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. “I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”

home.headline: Panthers’ Jalen Coker injury update is great news for TNF vs. Packers
home.blurb: Coker was a limited practice participant on Monday, sparking fears about his chances to play against the Packers due to a shoulder injury. While he’s not yet removed from the injury report, he’s now widely expected to eventually get cleared to see action versus Green Bay. The Carolina Panthers are looking to bounce back from a Week 7 loss as they share the field Thursday against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Green Bay. Carolina got some good news heading into that matchup, with wide receiver Jalen Coker practicing in full on Tuesday, according to the team’s latest injury report. The 24-year-old Coker is coming off a letdown performance. After racking up 97 receiving yards on six receptions and 13 targets in a 25-14 win on the road over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6, the former Holy Cross Crusaders star caught only one of four targets for nine receiving yards in a 43-13 demolition at the hands of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a Week 7 game on Sunday at home. Carolina’s attack was grounded as a whole in that contest by Tampa Bay, and it will be aiming to bounce back this Thursday in Titletown. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Coker is the other half of the Panthers’ top downfield duo in 2026 alongside wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan. On the season, Coker is second on the team with 328 receiving yards to go along with two touchdowns on 25 receptions and 39 targets. McMillan leads the Panthers with 511 receiving yards and two scores on 36 catches and 55 targets. As a team, the Bryce Young-led passing game of Carolina is second overall in the league with an average of 276.0 yards per outing. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. home.headline: Packers injury report: Jordan Love upgraded, 2 defensive starters added
home.blurb: Love, who is dealing with back soreness coming out of last Sunday's win over the Dallas Cowboys, got in a full padded practice on Thursday. He said Wednesday that he had no concerns over his availability for Sunday's showdown with the Detroit Lions , and Love's upgraded practice status on Thursday appears to confirm his belief. Barring a setback, he'll start against the Lions at Ford Field. Two defensive starters are dealing with new issues: Franklin has a shin injury, while Van Ness has an illness. It's currently unclear if either player is in danger of missing Sunday. More information will be available come Friday, when Matt LaFleur answers questions from the media before practice and before the Packers release a final injury report. Last week, safety Evan Williams was able to get through an illness and play well against the Cowboys. The only player who did not participate for the Packers at practice on Thursday was receiver Bo Melton, who is dealing with a back injury. He can be assumed out for Sunday unless he practices in some capacity on Friday. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle) and Matthew Golden (shoulder) both practiced in a limited capacity. LaFleur said both would play Sunday against the Lions. home.headline: Breaking down Packers' final injury report of Week 7 vs. Lions
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers listed left guard Aaron Banks, receiver Bo Melton, cornerback Benjamin St-Juste and defensive lineman Jordon Riley as questionable and ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin on the final injury report before facing the Detroit Lions in Week 7 of the 2026 season. LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): Banks got in a second week of practice and could be on the verge of his return to the field for the first time since injuring his toe in Week 2. If available, the Packers will have to determine if Banks or Laken Tomlinson -- who has started the last three games -- is the best option at left guard on Sunday. WR Bo Melton (back): After missing practices on Wednesday and Thursday, Melton returned in a limited capacity on Friday. The Packers could get by without him at receiver, but he's a core special teamer and a key player for covering kicks and punts. CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring): He didn't play last week after hurting his hamstring against the Bears , but he'll have a chance to return on Sunday after practicing all three days this week. St-Juste is a backup on the perimeter. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): Could he be ready to return? Riley has practiced the last two weeks. The Packers could use another capable player along the defensive front in a matchup against a top running back. LB Zaire Franklin (shin): The defensive's captain injured his shin during Thursday's practice and is out for Sunday. Expect Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper to start at linebacker. A matchup with Jahmyr Gibbs is a tough spot for two backup linebackers. The Lions listed defensive back Brian Branch and center Cade Mays as questionable. Both are coming off injury lists but were full participants at practice on Friday, and both will be expected to play on Sunday. How will the injury situation affect Sunday's NFC North showdown with the Lions? Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 7: Defensive lineman Anthony Campbell, cornerback Brandon Cisse, receiver Matthew Golden, quarterback Jordan Love, edge rusher Lukas Van Ness, receiver Christian Watson and receiver Savion Williams do not have a status designation on the final injury report and are good to go for Sunday. Love dealt with back soreness early in the week but was a full participant each of the final two days of practice. home.headline: Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons sounds off on NFL officials following team’s Week 7 loss to Lions
home.blurb: Josh Jacobs says he is remorseful in first comments since Packers return Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons sounds off on NFL officials following team’s Week 7 loss to Lions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers fell to the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon by the score of 20-17. Unfortunately, issues that have plagued the team all year, such as injuries, dropped passes, and missed kicks, reared their ugly heads again in Week Seven. Indeed, had the Packers played fundamental and mistake-free football, they would have won the game. After all, the Lions needed a field goal in the closing seconds of the contest in order to win. After the game was over, though, a great deal of criticism was directed at the NFL officials who refereed the game, including by one Packers player who was not able to participate: Micah Parsons . Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons criticizes NFL officials Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) celebrates his sack during the fourth quarter of their game Sunday, September 7, 2025 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Green Bay Packers beat the Detroit Lions 27-13. For their part, the Packers players themselves are not making excuses for the loss. That is, they are not at all saying that the reason they lost in Detroit was because of the officials. However, they are frustrated with the confusing calls made against them. Multiple players expressed their frustration about bogus roughing the passer calls while Jordan Love was mugged without any flags being thrown. They just want the game called fairly. Parsons, for his part, posted the following message on social media: This particular post is a reference, specifically, to how Brenton Cox was literally pushed into Lions quarterback Jared Goff and whistled for roughing the passer. Over the last several weeks, Green Bay players have been called for this penalty just for putting their hands on an opposing quarterback. At some point, something is going to have to change regarding how the officials are calling Packers games. Even the national media, including Tom Brady, thought the games was terrible in terms of how one-sided the referees were. The Packers won the game, 27-13. Game of Midweek: Panthers at Packers (-3.5, 47.5 o/u) Odds: -112 on bet365 Probability: 51.69% on ProphetX Thursday 8:15 p.m. ET, Amazon Prime Video The Panthers have taken over as the league's worst run defense, allowing 153.2 rushing yards per game. Although the Packers have been a pass-first team, they can get back on track with more balance in this matchup. The promising return of Josh Jacobs last week will lead to an even bigger game from the workhorse. The Panthers' offense is suddenly hurting and facing a more inspired Jonathan Gannon defense on the road doesn't bode well. Pick: Packers win 27-17 and cover the spread. Steven Bisig - IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFC Game of the Week: Bears at Seahawks (-3.5, 46.5 o/u) Odds: +104 on bet365 Probability: 48.31% on ProphetX Monday 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN The Bears have been a scoring machine when quarterback Caleb Williams leads their explosive offense. The Seahawks , however, can contain D'Andre Swift in the running game to set up more pressure chances to get at Williams. The Bears' defense will keep them in it with some sacks and takeaways vs. Sam Darnold. In a lower-scoring affair in prime time, go with the team backed by a loud home crowd. Pick: Seahawks win 23-20 but fail to cover the spread. AFC Game of the Week: Chiefs (-1.5, 41.5 o/u) at Broncos Odds: -110 on bet365 Probability: 50.74% on ProphetX Sunday 4:25 p.m. ET, CBS The Chiefs were shell-shocked by their shellacking in Seattle, but they will have a chance to rebound on the ground with Kenneth Walker III. Bo Nix has been a great home QB but Patrick Mahomes also has a history of owning the Broncos . This should be a hard-fought physical game but Kansas City's running game will provide the winning edge. Pick: Chiefs win 23-20 and cover the spread. Lock of the Week: Colts at Jaguars (-7.5, 46.5 o/u) Odds: -111 on bet365 Probability: 52.15% on ProphetX Sunday 1 p.m. ET, CBS The Jaguars are an interception-hungry defense under Anthony Campanile. Daniel Jones is struggling with ball protection and making bad decisions like he did in his Giants ' days. Jacksonville will be ready to fly out of the gate after a Week 7 bye, while Indianapolis is reeling and almost going through the motions with lame-duck coach Shane Steichen. The Jaguars also are No. 1 against the run, making it tougher sledding for Jonathan Taylor. Pick: Jaguars win 31-14 and cover the spread. Upset of the Week: Falcons (+1.5, 46.5 o/u) at Buccaneers Odds: -103 on bet365 Probability: 49.26% on ProphetX Atlanta and Tampa Bay, like the rest of the shaky NFC South, are roller coaster, box-of-chocolate teams. You never know what you'll get, especially when division rivals play each other, regardless of who's home and who's away. We think the Buccaneers (routing the Panthers on the road) were impressive in Week 7, but the Falcons made the bigger statement (beating the 49ers at home). That's all we've got and we're going with it. Pick: Falcons win 27-24. Ravens at Bills (-3.5, 53.5 o/u) Odds: -104 on bet365 Probability: 48.08% on ProphetX The Bills have more issues with pass defense, but whether it's Tyler Huntley or Lamar Jackson, the Ravens give them a break with their inconsistency. Derrick Henry has been a Bills killer in the past, but Baltimore's rushing attack is slumping. Buffalo is home and well-rested after a bye and can lean into Josh Allen's great passing and running history against Baltimore. He will improve to 5-3 vs. the Ravens. Pick: Bills win 31-24 and cover the spread. Titans at Bengals (-10.5, 46.5 o/u) The Titans are hoping Cam Ward can keep flashing why he was the No. 1 overall pick as their franchise QB. The Bengals don't have those questions with Joe Burrow, who is red-hot in picking apart pass defenses. Burrow is locked into his wide receivers and tight ends as a potential MVP. Ward will face Dexter Lawrence and a much-improved defensive front on the road. Pick: Bengals win 34-17 and cover the spread. Cardinals at Cowboys (-6.5, 53.5 o/u) Odds: -105 on bet365 Probability: 50.5% on ProphetX Sunday 1 p.m. ET, Fox The Cardinals have had almost zero chance to win at home for a while but they are more comfortable on the road. The Cowboys, however, tend to dominate non-prime window games at home. Their defense gets a break from a compressed passing game and a hurting running game. Arizona, on the flipside, cannot cover or contain Dak Prescott's weapons downfield. Pick: Cowboys win 30-20 and cover the spread. Vikings at Lions (-3.5, 46.5 o/u) Odds: -102 on bet365 Probability: 47.85% on ProphetX The Vikings have dominated with defense and are getting away with little offense. They will face a different kind of test on the road. Jared Goff can handle blitzes well with his top wide receivers and tight ends. Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions' running game can also get some wins at the line of scrimmage. The Lions' defense also carries some positive vibes after slowing down the Packers. Pick: Lions win 23-20 but fail to cover the spread. Raiders (-1.5, 44.5 o/u) at Jets Odds: +106 on bet365 Probability: 49.02% on ProphetX The Raiders are sticking with Kirk Cousins after four consecutive losses. They are at least competitive offensively and have some defensive playmakers. The Jets, however, are a little more desperate as Aaron Glenn feels more heat. Geno Smith is still feeling it with the new-look offense and the defense gets a break because the Raiders' running game tends to sputter. Pick: Jets win 24-20. Browns at Steelers (-3.5, 38.5 o/u) Probability: 50.98% on ProphetX The Browns have all their five wins thanks to Deshaun Watson snatching victory from the jaws of defeat late in the fourth quarter. That's a feel-good development for rookie coach Todd Monken, but not sustainable as a first-place team. Aaron Rodgers is feeling it since the last Cleveland matchup and will outduel Watson with superior weapons. Pick: Steelers win 24-20 and cover the spread. Chargers at Rams (-6.5, 43.5 o/u) Odds: -113 on bet365 Probability: 52.83% on ProphetX Sunday 4:05 p.m. ET, Fox Justin Herbert and Jim Harbaugh lead the league's only winless team in Week 8. They should fix some issues and come out with a cleaner, run-heavy offense. Herbert should have his best game of the season after the bye, which doesn't require much. The Rams also have been sloppy at times. The Rams survive another scare in the battle for Los Angeles. Pick: Rams win 27-23 but fail to cover the spread. Matt Marton-Imagn Images Patriots (-7.5, 44.5 o/u) at Dolphins Odds: -108 on bet365 The Patriots' offense had a hiccup with Drake Maye in Chicago, but he should get back on track against a Dolphins defense giving up plenty of his signature big pass plays. New England can also keep running the ball well and the defense will respond better for Mike Vrabel. Miami got on the board last week and there will be a division letdown this week. Pick: Patriots win 24-14 and cover the spread. Eagles at Commanders (-3.5, 40.5 o/u) Odds: -114 on bet365 Probability: 55.16% on ProphetX Sunday 8:20 p.m. ET, NBC/Peacock The Commanders are fighting through some offensive line and skill injuries but Jayden Daniels should come out a little more settled in the David Blough offense after the bye. The Eagles' defense has become a little more vulnerable and their offense is down to being run-heavy against a good Washington run defense under Dan Quinn. Pick: Commanders win 20-17 but fail to cover the spread. clearly need him back. They got out to a 13-0 lead in Week 7, a week Jackson seemed very likely to suit up for. But they blew the lead, and now sit at 4-3. Will the Ravens get Jackson back for Week 8 when they face off against the Buffalo Bills ? It's hard to say with the shaky nature of this ankle injury for Jackson, but on Tuesday, the Ravens got some good news. According to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport , Jackson is expected to play in Week 8 against the Bills. For the first time since his ankle injury, Jackson is close to 100% healthy, which bodes well for his odds to suit up this upcoming week. Ravens get good news on Lamar Jackson for Week 8 "First of all, I expect based on the people I've spoken with that Lamar Jackson will play this week," Rapoport said. "He'll be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills." From @BigDayESPN: #Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is expected to return to the field this week. That, plus a little more on his fun press conference. https://t.co/AKQSjjAy5U There is finally some good news for the Ravens on the Jackson injury front, as he's seemingly finally set to come back and suit up for Baltimore in Week 8. He's missed three games with an ankle injury, but is closing in on a return to the field for Week 8. While it's not yet confirmed by the Ravens or Jackson, this report is a huge sign things are trending in the right direction. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ’ Jonathan Taylor Rapoport added to his report, revealing that "He is believed to be as close to 100% as he's been, and the Ravens do expect him to play." With Rapoport reporting that Jackson is expected to play and that he's close to being 100% for this week's upcoming matchup against the Bills, it seems likely Jackson is good to go. Facing the Bills in Week 8, the Ravens are expected to have Jackson back at quarterback over Tyler Huntley. It's not yet official, but this is the most positive sign that Jackson is coming back. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Ravens odds: Opening lines for Week 8 matchup | Buffalo Rumblings Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Buffalo Bills Community Buffalo Rumblings October 28, 2026 Buffalo Rumblings Notifications Notifications Sections Buffalo Rumblinks By/For Fans The Feed Community Guidelines Today's Trivia Betting Betting News FanDuel NFL Odds FanDuel Super Bowl Odds Buffalo Bills Odds NFL Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search Sections Expand Buffalo Rumblinks By/For Fans Expand The Feed Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Buffalo Bills Odds The Buffalo Bills and Josh Allen renew their rivalry with the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8 The Buffalo Bills are back in action for Week 8 after a bye that proved fruitful for their overall standing in both the AFC East and the AFC in general. Following a two-game west coast road stand where they picked up wins against the Los Angeles Rams and Las Vegas Raiders, the Bills are back in Orchard Park, NY and ready to welcome the Baltimore Ravens at the new Highmark Stadium. At 5-1, Buffalo now shares a piece of first place in the AFC, while Baltimore is stuck in the AFC North basement with a 4-3 record. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook expect a close game, with the Bills currently 3.5-point favorites (-3.5) over the Ravens . Buffalo’s defense has struggled to stop opposing offenses in most games to this point in the season, and Baltimore just gave up 35 points to the Cincinnati Bengals. Could we see a high-scoring affair this coming Sunday? The current odds don’t expect a track meet, with the over/under set at O/U 53.5. It’s going to be important to be tuned-in to both teams’ injury throughout the week. Of significance for the Bills is whether or not wide receiver DJ Moore (AC joint sprain) and defensive tackle Ed Oliver (hip) are healthy enough to suit up in Week 8. The Ravens’ biggest concerns continues to be the health of quarterback Lamar Jackson, who has missed the last three games due to a high ankle sprain. This will be the 15th game in the all-time series between Buffalo and (the current) Baltimore, with each team having won 7 games in that span. The Bills and quarterback Josh Allen are 4-3 against the Ravens since 2018, which includes a pair of playoff wins. Buffalo and Baltimore last sparred in primetime during Week 1 of the 2025 NFL season. The Bills pulled off an incredible comeback win late in the fourth quarter set in motion by Ed Oliver’s forced fumble of running back Derrick Henry. With just over four minutes left, Allen got to work in guiding Buffalo’s offense to 16 unanswered points and a 41-40 win to start the season. picks.headline: 1 Bold Prediction for Each Game in NFL Week 8, Including Ravens-Bills
picks.blurb: 1 Bold Prediction for Each Game in NFL Week 8, Including Ravens-Bills Opens in a new tab NFL NFL Schedule NFL Power Rankings NFL Defense Rankings NFL Offense Rankings NFL QB Rankings MLB MLB Standings MLB Power Rankings NBA NBA Playoffs Bracket NBA Power Rankings 50 Best NBA Players NHL NHL Standings NHL Power Rankings NASCAR NASCAR Standings NASCAR Power Rankings UFC Men's Pound for Pound Rankings Women's Pound for Pound Rankings COLLEGE College Basketball College Football Other College Sports NFL News, Rumors & Analysis Add Sportsnaut on Google Add on Google Facebook Credit: USA TODAY Sports Even though the last game just ended on Monday, the football calendar moves fast, and now it’s time to look ahead to Week 8, which kicks off on Thursday. With 28 of 32 teams back in action, it’s time to make a bold prediction for all 14 games on the NFL Week 8 schedule. Related: 5 NFL Trades That Could Happen Before Nov. 10 Deadline Packers Hold Panthers to Season-Low 10 Points The Green Bay Packers’ defense has been trending in the right direction, and they don’t even have Micah Parsons back yet. Jonathan Gannon is pressing all the right buttons, and that will continue, even against a top-scoring Carolina Panthers offense that struggled last week. While Bryce Young has been excellent this season, he’ll stumble a bit this week against Green Bay, leading to a season-low 10 points for Carolina. Josh Allen/Lamar Jackson Combine for 700 Yards and 6 Touchdowns as Bills Beat Ravens Week 8 matches up two of the best teams in the AFC in what could be a Conference Championship preview. Both boasting former NFL MVPs, each will show off their respective talents and combine for a ridiculous 700 yards and six touchdowns, giving fans plenty of excitement. But this time it will be Josh Allen’s Buffalo Bills who topple Lamar Jackson’s Baltimore Ravens. He’s beaten the Ravens in four of seven attempts (including 2-of-2 in the postseason), but now that John Harbaugh isn’t there, Allen will have an easier time. Bengals Score 45 Points in Big Win Over Titans It still feels like the Cincinnati Bengals haven’t played to their full potential. We could see it all come together against a woefully bad Tennessee Titans team that has really struggled to move the ball. The Bengals’ defense is not only doing a better job of keeping opponents out of the end zone, they’re forcing more turnovers too. Overall, this could be one of the easiest games of the season for the Bengals Cardinals Beat Cowboys With Season-High 150 Rushing Yards Jeremiyah Love hasn’t been the instant superstar some thought he’d become. Yet, the Arizona Cardinals may have unexpectedly found another impact running back with Bam Knight. With Knight and Love working in tandem and possibly hitting their stride against one of the NFL’s worst run defenses, the Cardinals could go off for a season-high 150 rushing yards. Related: 5 Josh Sweat Trade Destinations After NFL Rumors Heat Up Vikings Score 40 Points in Convincing Win Over Lions The Minnesota Vikings may have had a slow start to their season offensively, but the defense and special teams have always been reliable. The same can’t be said about the Detroit Lions’ defense, which has been one of the worst in football. With Kyler Murray now having more time on task, the Vikings are ready to show off Kevin O’Connell’s vision in adding the former No. 1 overall pick to an offense that features Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson. While the Lions can score plenty of points, the Vikings will go off for a season-high 40 points against a Detroit D that just can’t get right. Related: 5 Minnesota Vikings Trades To Capitalize on Hot Start Brock Bowers’ Career-High 150 Yards Helps Raiders Beat Jets Brock Bowers is one of the NFL’s best tight ends and is easily the Las Vegas Raiders’ top target. Surprisingly, his career-high of 140 yards came back in 2024 as a rookie. But now he has his best quarterback yet, and if Kirk Cousins feeds him enough, Bowers could set a new personal best with a massive 150-yard game to beat the New York Jets. T.J. Watt Ends Game on Deshaun Watson Strip-Sack, Clinching Steelers Win Over Browns Former NFL Defensive Player of the Year T.J. Watt is what many refer to as a closer. He’s the type of talent who can wreak havoc on an opponent’s game plan. That’s exactly what he’ll do in Todd Monken’s first visit to Acrisure Stadium as the Cleveland Browns’ head coach by forcing a strip-sack on Deshaun Watson to seal a Steelers victory. The Browns won the first game of the series at home, so now it’s the Steelers’ turn to do the same on their grass. Related: 5 Jerry Jeudy Landing Spots After NFL Trade Rumors Heat Up Buccaneers Rack Up 450 Yards of Offense In Win Over Falcons The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally have Baker Mayfield back in the starting lineup, and his thumb is feeling closer to normal. While the Atlanta Falcons could test the Buccaneers’ limits on both sides of the ball, this one could get into a high-scoring affair. If so, the Buccaneers just might put together their most complete offensive performance of the season, going off for 450 yards of offense after getting a taste of success last week against Carolina. Related: 4 Vita Vea Trade Destinations Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline Bhayshul Tuten’s 100-Yard Game Helps Jaguars Race Past Colts Now a second-year pro, the former fourth-round pick is having a career year. But he still hasn’t had a game with 100 yards from scrimmage. That will change this week against an already bad Indianapolis Colts defense that could be missing a few extra pieces by the time Sunday’s game kicks off. Related: 11 Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Solutions After NFL Rumors Emerge Chargers Get Season’s First Win on Last-Second Field Goal Against Rams It’s hard out there for a Los Angeles Chargers fan. Going into the season with playoff expectations, there’s nothing that a win in Week 8 will do to lift spirits. Though, perhaps beating the team that entered the season with Super Bowl expectations could help everyone involved in the Chargers’ dumpster fire feel a little better about themselves, even if it’s too late to matter. Related: 6 Khalil Mack Trade Destinations As NFL Rumors Heat Up Chiefs Defense Forces Three Turnovers From Bo Nix in Broncos Loss Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos’ offense isn’t intimidating anyone this season. They’re certainly not scaring an experienced Super Bowl-winning defensive coordinator like Steve Spagnuolo. The Kansas City Chiefs’ defensive coach could turn up the heat on Nix, knowing they’re not exactly prone to explosive plays. While Nix usually does a good job taking care of the football, there’s been a lot of outside noise lately, and perhaps this is the week he cracks. Related: 5 Jonathan Taylor Trade Destinations That Make Sense Before NFL Deadline A.J. Brown’s 130-Yard, 2 TD Day Helps Patriots Sink Dolphins A.J. Brown hasn’t quite been able to dominate with the New England Patriots like he once did before things got awkward with Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles. Though, he is coming off his best one yet, a three-reception, 48-yard performance last Thursday night. Could the Patriots look to foster that relationship against one of the NFL’s worst secondaries on Sunday? Taking on the Miami Dolphins, this could be Brown’s breakout game with the Patriots. Jayden Daniels’ 350-Yard-Day Helps Commanders Clip Eagles Jayden Daniels has shown everything this year. Not only has he brought up durability issues by missing two games due to injury, but he’s also flashed his superstar talent as a passer with a 300-yard game and as a rusher with a 100-yard game. Now he’ll have a game where he puts it all together, putting fear in the Philadelphia Eagles by air and with his legs. Related: 5 Philadelphia Eagles QB Trade Targets After Jalen Hurts Hits IR, Including One Franchise’s Star Cairo Santos’ Missed Kick Helps Seahawks Beat Bears Last week, Cairo Santos set a new career-high with his 58-yard game-sealing kick. But he also missed a 53-yarder earlier in the fourth quarter. Now he’ll be back in primetime for the second week in a row. Only this time, his attempt at a game-winning kick will go awry, leading to the Seattle Seahawks taking down Ben Johnson’s team. away.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson expected to play in Week 8: report
away.blurb: Jackson was able to notch limited practice participation leading up to this past Sunday’s Week 7 loss to the Bengals, but he was ultimately ruled out. Now, the Ravens are gearing up for a highly-anticipated Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed each of the last three games after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that span with Tyler Huntley at the helm, dropping each of their last two games against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Tuesday, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport confidently reported that Jackson will be on the field for this Week 8 clash. “I expect, based on the people that I’ve spoken with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week. He will be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills,” Rapoport said. “I know we’ve been here before. This was a 2-3 week injury — he’s through the third week. He is believed to be as close to 100% as he has been and the Ravens do expect him to play.” With Jackson off the field, the Ravens have dropped to last place in the AFC North standings with a 4-3 record. They’ll look to get back in the win column in a difficult road matchup against the Bills this coming Sunday. Sunday’s game will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. The Ravens then have a short week to prepare for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. Right now, on FanDuel , the Bengals are a 10.5-point favorite against the Titans. Their moneyline is -650, and the over/under is 46.5 points. This will be Tennessee’s first time playing in Cincinnati since 2020. Ironically, that was Week 8 in 2020 and on November 1st. The Bengals won that game 31-20, which was a coming-out party for Joe Burrow in his rookie season. Burrow was 26/37 for 249 yards and two touchdowns in that game, making a featured appearance on the highlights during NBC’s Sunday Night Football game coverage that night. Since that game, the Bengals and Titans have played four times in Nashville, including in the Divisional round of the 2021 NFL Playoffs. That was the game where Joe Burrow overcame nine sacks and willed the Bengals to a 19-16 win that was the first road playoff win in Bengals history. Cincinnati beat Tennessee 37-27 in Week 15 of the 2024 Season, which was the most recent matchup between the two teams. Tennessee’s head coach is Robert Saleh, in his first season with the Titans. He previously coached the New York Jets and served two stints as the San Francisco 49ers’ defensive coordinator. The Titans are 1-6 and coming off a last-second 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Quarterback Cam Ward is in his second season and has thrown for just 1,179 yards and just four touchdowns this season. Ward also has just one game with over 200 passing yards. Entering Sunday, the Titans were in the bottom two in the NFL in both scoring and total offense, while ranking in the middle of the pack in both scoring and total defense. However, the Titans have been competitive most of the season, as four of their six losses came by one score. Two of them were to the division-leading Giants (12-7) and the aforementioned loss to Cleveland. If the Bengals come out like they did in the first half at Baltimore, the Titans can make them uncomfortable for four quarters. Who Dey! Join Bengals fans on the SB Nation app! home.headline: Bengals place tight end, feared to have torn ACL, on injured reserve: report
home.blurb: All suffered the injury during the Bengals’ 35-13 rout of the Ravens on Sunday in Baltimore and was ruled out at the beginning of the fourth quarter. He had three catches for 26 yards before leaving with his injury. The Bengals have already lost one tight end to a season-ending injury. Tanner Hudson suffered a torn pectoral earlier in October, and he is out for the year. CINCINNATI, Ohio — The Bengals placed third-year tight end Erick All Jr. on injured reserve on Tuesday with a knee injury. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport , the team believes that All has a torn ACL. In corresponding moves, the Bengals signed TE Cam Grandy from the Vikings’ practice squad, placed TE Josh Kattus on the practice squad/injured list and signed TE Caden Prieskorn to the practice squad. All, a fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, had returned to the field this season after tearing his ACL in 2024, an injury that also cost him all of last season. He has eight receptions on the season for 56 yards. Grandy had been with the Bengals each of the previous two seasons, catching seven passes for 35 yards. The Bengals waived him in August, and he joined Minnesota’s practice squad. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

home.blurb: Your Privacy Choices/(Opt-Out of Sale/Targeted Ads) Cincinnati Bengals tight end Erick All Jr. has reportedly suffered another knee injury that could end his 2026 season. On Tuesday, the Bengals placed All, 26, on injured reserve. According to multiple reports, including from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and ESPN, All is believed to have suffered a torn ACL during the Bengals’ win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. All missed the entirety of the 2025 season due to an ACL tear, and, if confirmed, this would be the third tear of his right ACL, with the first occurring while he was playing college football at Iowa. The Bengals signed tight end Cam Grandy to the active roster in the wake of All’s injury. Through six games this season, All collected eight catches for 56 yards. Sunday was All’s best game of the season, hauling in three catches for 26 yards. NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers: Seahawks Spoil Kenneth Walker III’s Return to Seattle Cardinals' Injury Report is Downright Ugly Skip to main content SI.COM ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals revealed their Thursday injury report for Week 7's clash against the Denver Broncos — and it's not pretty. Darius Robinson and Jon Gaines were added to an already lengthy list of Cardinals that featured Walter Nolen, Budda Baker and Jeremiyah Love among others. Cardinals Thursday Injury Report FULL : Isaac Seumalo (rest), Josh Sweat (rest), Jedrick Wills (illness), The Cardinals, hoping to again play the role of spoiler against Denver, could be massively shorthanded in making that happen as numerous stars are staring down a legitimate possibility of missing time. Baker, Love, Wingard and Nolen have all missed consecutive days of practice now for Arizona. With the Cardinals hoping to take advantage of a disfunctional Broncos offense, Arizona's defense needs all hands on deck. “Last few years. They’re very smart. They’re very well coached," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of the Broncos' defense. "I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them. You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it. "They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. Yes, it’s the last two weeks, but it’s really been all year, and it’s been for a few years now. We have our hands full with this group, for sure.” Published Oct 23, 2026 DONNIE DRUIN Donnie Druin is the Publisher for Arizona Cardinals and Phoenix Suns On SI. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. picks.headline: Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8
picks.blurb: Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rays rally, avoid sweep Anthony Edwards injury NFL Power Rankings WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Jayson Tatum buzzer-beater Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 27, 2026 at 2:38 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Minnesota Vikings plan their next massive blitz, the Detroit Lions ride the wave of a big division win. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFC North clash. It's a critical game for the Lions. The NFC North could end up with only two playoff teams. That's because the 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams still seem like firm bets. And that leaves only one other Wild Card spot. The Lions stand at 4-2 while the Vikings are 6-0. A loss would leave the Lions three games back of first place with nearly half the season in the rearview mirror. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs will rush for 100-plus yards It's tough to throw against the Vikings. They rank No. 2 in the NFL against the pass, allowing just 155 yards per game. And while their run defense is good, it's still the better path to consistently moving the football. Gibbs is fourth in the NFL with 620 yards through six games. Look for the Lions to put a saddle on him against the Vikings. Yes, the Lions are clearly overusing Gibbs already. He's almost on a record pace , according to NBC Sports. "If Gibbs keeps to his current pace of 27.7 touches per game for the entire 17-game season, he'll finish this season with a whopping 470 touches," Michael David Smith wrote. "That would be the second-most in a season in NFL history, second only to former James Wilder, who had 492 touches with the 1984 Buccaneers." Gibbs should get close to that number of touches on the ground alone. He had 29 carries against the Saints and Packers this season. Look for the neighborhood of 25 against the Vikings. He's averaging 4.6 per carry, so that easily puts him over 100. And don't worry about the injury scare late against the Packers, according to mlive.com. During his postgame media session, Lions coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Gibbs is OK and avoided serious injury . "Yeah, we got him checked," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. "He should be good. That's that whole, 'Is it really worth going down and try to finish the game, or you just go score?' Sometimes I question that. I don't know, maybe we shouldn't just, but all good. It's a good win." Lions will double the Vikings' season average in points allowed For the season, the Vikings are allowing just 12.3 points per game. Over the last three games, they are giving up just 33 points. But the Lions will hit them for 24-plus points. Not only will Gibbs cut loose, but his runs will set up play-action daggers for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. This is no timid prediction. The Vikings defense is the real deal. The players will even tell you that , according to The Athletic. "It's a generational group," cornerback Isaiah Rodgers said. "We've got guys who go out and trust the scheme. They trust (Flores and his staff). The stats speak for themselves." Defensive tackle Levi Drake Rodriguez said it is togetherness that brings the good outcomes. "Hopefully, that showed the joy we have on the field with each other," Rodriguez said. "We want to work hard for each other. We want to be right." But the Lions are a different beast. They are king of the offensive jungle for a reason. They rank No. 2 in the NFL with 397.3 yards per game. The NFL used to be a league where great defense would pretty much always shut down a great offense. But the rules have changed. And the Lions will cut loose for a point total the Vikings haven't allowed since 22 in the season opener against the Packers. Vikings QB Kyler Murray will have his best game of the season For all the Lions are on offense, they ain't that on defense. They rank dead last in the league with 391 yards allowed per game. Murray hasn't thrown for 250 yards in a game yet this season. In fact, he hasn't done it since 2024. And he only has three touchdown passes in basically four games played. He missed almost all of the season opener after a first-quarter injury. But the Lions are relatively decent against the run. They are an open gate against the pass. And Murray will take advantage with some chunk plays down the field. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is standing behind Murray, according to The Athletic. "I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far-off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going." One reason for optimism is that Murray has gotten better at play action. The Vikings used play action on nearly half of Murray's dropbacks in Week 7. And Murray hit on eight of 11 passes. There's still hope for Murray. Some people have been writing him off and saying the Vikings should move on, but this is a chance for him to silence critics. Why do we allow the numbers six and four to dominate our lives like this? On this NFL Sunday morning, I'm here to resist with a three-pack of bold predictions as we careen violently toward kickoff. The streets are saying I just didn't have time to make a six-pack, to which I will tell the streets to shut up because they're literally just made of concrete while I am a luminous being, not this crude matter. The NFC North will feature heavily, and I have more words for Bo Nix; should be a three-packtacular time! The Vikings will blow it against the Colts to lose undefeated streak Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and wide receiver Justin Jefferson | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect But hey, this is bold predictions, not "pick a touchdown favorite to win" predictions, and the ultimate zag here would be to say that the Colts, who have launched an exploratory committee on trading their entire team , shock everyone by inverting the vibes completely. There isn't a great argument for this to happen, otherwise it wouldn't be bold, but there is an argument. The Vikings offense really is terrible; they are 27th in EPA per play ahead of absolute titans like the ... Tennessee Titans, the Miami Dolphins and the Los Angeles Chargers. They have had real difficulty moving the ball with Kyler Murray under center, and have gimmicked their way to wins with timely turnovers and crazy performance from an aggressive defense. I'm not saying that doesn't work (it clearly works), but there's no way it can work this consistently. The Colts need to stabilize behind their strengths: running the football and managing an efficient offensive attack. In Week 6 against the Titans, it felt like they held some emergency war council meeting at halftime where they all pitched their best ideas on how to best lose the game. If the team can just play to its own strengths rather than allow their weaknesses to consume them, they should have a chance. Bo Nix will be benched in the third quarter against Arizona Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This is what we call putting the "bold" and "prediction" in bold prediction, because I could have just said something like "Bo Nix will play garbage football again and we'll all hop on our podcasts and blogs and wonder what he does," but let's get real cynical. What if the Broncos and Sean Payton lose their patience completely? Bo Nix is not a good quarterback. I don't know if he's bad, but by every metric imaginable and by the evidence of my own two eyeballs he's been remarkably ineffective this year. He can't really throw over the middle and he can't really throw deep down the sideline, so he basically just runs a college offense with a ton of handoffs, screen passes and dumpoffs with a hysterically low average depth of target. I don't think Jarrett Stidham is any better, nor am I one of those clowns constantly canvassing for unproven backups to start with no evidence that they'll be good. What I know is that the Broncos coaching staff agrees with my assessment of Bo Nix -they trust him with nothing, refuse to call any downfield shots and just try to protect, protect, protect for as long as they can while they win the game with runs, field goals and defense. If they somehow fall down big to Arizona, though? Maybe we see some emergency quarterback switch, if for no other reason than to save face with the rest of the team. Lions defense shows improvement off the bye, limits Green Bay in a big win at home Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Lions defense, so far this year, has been USDA-certified garbage. They have yet to hold a team under 20 points, get cleaved by every elite pass-catcher they encounter and had one of the most unprofessional performances I ever did see on Thursday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills in Week 2. But I, in my infinite wisdom, have decided (for some reason) that this all will get better, and it will get better right now. This is for three reasons: First, the Lions are getting Brian Branch back for the first time all year, a keystone defensive player and the kind of guy they've been missing all season. Second, they're at home, and home field still really matters in football for defensive performance -the only sport where it still really means anything. Third and finally is simple mathematical regression. No defense is in reality this unprofessional, and it's likely if not guaranteed that some of the early-season miscommunications that made the Lions defense so terrible have been ironed out. That's probably factored into the betting line, which is fascinating: Detroit is favored by 3.5 points. They're at home, and their offense is as good as it gets, but Vegas does not buy the Packers recent hot streak at all. Give me the Lions. The over/under for this one currently rests at 46.5 points. On Sunday, the Vikings once again struggled on offense against a team that they probably shouldn’t have struggled against on offense, as they managed to get into the end zone just one time against the Indianapolis Colts. Thanks to another stellar performance by the defense, however, that was enough, as they managed to hold on for a 16-10 victory to push their record to 6-0. With the San Francisco 49ers losing to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon and the Kansas City Chiefs falling to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday Night Football, the Vikings are now the only team in the league that still has a donut in the loss column. Week 7 in Detroit saw a game of “You take it. . .no, you take it” between the Lions and another NFC North rival of ours, the Green Bay Packers. The game featured bad interceptions on both sides and the standard dumb Dan Campbell fourth-down decision, going for it on 4th-and-1 from his own 24-yard line in a 17-17 game with five minutes remaining. That failed fourth down was immediately followed by Green Bay kicker Trey Smack having a 35-yard field goal attempt blocked to preserve the tie. The Lions then pushed the ball down the field far enough for Jake Bates to kick the game-winning field goal and help the Lions escape with a 20-17 win. away.headline: Vikings get positive injury update on RB Aaron Jones: report
away.blurb: The veteran ball carrier exited the game in the fourth quarter as the Vikings posted 10 unanswered points to secure a 16-10 win over the visiting Colts. He was listed as questionable to return, but did not. Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones left Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts with a knee injury. Fortunately for the Vikings, this injury for Jones doesn’t appear to be serious. On Monday, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported a positive update on the Vikings RB. “Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as ‘day to day,'” Schefter reported. This injury for Jones occurred in the same game that fellow running back Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve. Mason missed each of the Vikings’ last four games after suffering a thumb injury in Week 1, forcing Jones to step up as the team’s bell-cow lead back. Mason led the Vikings in rushing on Sunday, taking 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones recording 26 yards on eight carries before exiting the game. The Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, boasting a 6-0 recording heading into this coming Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions. away.headline: Detroit Lions sign former Vikings DL to practice squad, release WR
away.blurb: Originally an undrafted free agent by the Vikings in 2024 out of Oregon , Taimani finished with 22 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one quarterback hurry, and one fumble recovery during the 2023 college football season with the Ducks. As Sunday's NFC North showdown approaches, the Detroit Lions (4-2) signed former Minnesota Vikings (6-0) defensive lineman Taki Taimani to their practice squad on Tuesday. Taimani, a 6-foot-1, 309-pound lineman, has appeared in nine NFL games (all with the Vikings ) and has registered four tackles. Per Pro Football Focus , Taimani logged 70 defensive snaps in 2024 and carded a 61.2 overall defensive grade that season. In 2025, Taimani tallied just 35 defensive snaps and had an overall defensive grade of 27.4 last season from PFF . In its corresponding move, the Lions released wide receiver Lawrence Keys from their practice squad. Detroit signed Keys back in June after a stint in the UFL with the Houston Gamblers. The 5-foot-11, 170-pound receiver finished second in the UFL with 1,001 all-purpose yards over the Gamblers' 10-game schedule. Keys registered 349 receiving yards on 24 receptions including two touchdown catches. The 26-year-old also returned 19 kickoffs for 518 yards and 11 punts for 134 yards and a 12.2 average, which ranked third in the league. After going undrafted in 2024, Keys signed with the Buffalo Bills . But, he was released prior to the start of the 2024 NFL season. During his college career at Notre Dame and then Tulane, Keys caught 81 passes for 1,080 yards and nine touchdowns. Keys' most productive collegiate season was 2023 when he hauled in 30 passes for 296 yards and two scores. Keys was waived by the Lions in August during training camp with an injury settlement before signing back onto the practice squad in late September. away.headline: Vikings-Colts Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, only Jordan Mason has an injury designation, but his questionable designation is a technical one for those coming off of IR. He will play on Sunday. Christian Darrisaw and Harrison Smith had their customary rest days on Friday. For the Colts, a total of seven players have injury designations. The most significant are starting cornerback Sauce Gardner and starting tight end Tyler Warren, both of whom are out, as is wide receiver Anthony Gould. Starting linebacker Bryce Boettcher is questionable, as is his backup C.J. Allen, which could leave them thin at the position. The same is true at cornerback with Sauce Gardner out and Justin Walley questionable. Lastly, punter Rigoberto Sanchez did not practice all week and is listed as questionable. The Colts added a punter to their roster this week in case he can’t go on Sunday. home.blurb: Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire Skip to main content SI.COM Cooper, of course, is on injured reserve with a torn Achilles. Franklin suffered an injured shin at practice on Thursday and is out on the Packers’ final injury report. Franklin was the only player ruled out by LaFleur on the injury report. Left guard Aaron Banks, receiver Bo Melton, defensive tackle Jordon Riley and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste are questionable. Star safety Brian Branch said he’s “ready to roll” as he makes his debut following last season’s torn Achilles. Officially, he is questionable. “I’m really excited, to be honest,” he told reporters in Detroit. “Play the game that you love that you've been missing out for so long. To come back like this is a blessing to be able to play this game. I'm just going to execute [the game plan] and, if I execute, it's going to be a hell of a game.” Questionable: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), WR Bo Melton (back), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring). Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. Questionable: S Brian Branch (Achilles), C Cade Mays (wrist). Branch has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. DETROIT – There’s never a good time to play without your starting linebackers. That’s especially true for the Green Bay Packers, who will play without premier starter Edgerrin Cooper and defensive captain Zaire Franklin for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions. It’s not exactly ideal considering the Lions are second in the NFL in scoring, fourth in total offense and have a premier running back with Jahmyr Gibbs. “Unfortunate deal,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Friday’s practice. “That happens when you play football, especially the way our guys have been practicing.” Quarterback Jordan Love (back) and cornerback Brandon Cisse (stinger) are among those off the final injury report. Melton missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday but returned on Friday. Riley remains on injured reserve but just completed his second week of practice. Banks hasn’t played since his one and only game against the Jets in Week 2. St-Juste was inactive last week. “Big, stout physical D-lineman. Exactly what we need,” coach Matt LaFleur said of Riley before practice. As expected , unning back Josh Jacobs appears ready to make his debut after being removed from the exempt list this week. The NFL gave him a one-week roster exemption, so he will have to be activated by 3 p.m. Saturday, which is the same deadline for any other roster moves, such as activating Riley or practice-squad elevations. “Yeah, I believe so,” LaFleur said of Jacobs being ready. “But we’ll get through it and see how he’s feeling and the confidence he has in himself, which I think is pretty strong. home.blurb: St. Brown has not been injured much. Aside from meaningless Week 18 games, you do not see him missing many games. He has 89 career games active in his sixth NFL season. So, while Campbell is hesitant to say for certain that he will play, his track record combined with the severity of the injury makes it sound like the team is holding him out of caution. St. Brown Breaks Out Against Packers St. Brown came out of the bye fresh and performed well. The hope is that he is not going to miss any time. If Detroit wants to have any chance of winning the division, they have to find a way to win this game. So, the team should see St. Brown playing. They also have three division games after Week 15 and two division games to close out the season. Lions HC Reveals Amon-Ra St. Brown Injury Update - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Lions HC Reveals Amon-Ra St. Brown Injury Update Amon-Ra St. Brown Getty Parker Hurley Mon, October 26, 2026 at 11:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown missed a little time in the win over the Green Bay Packers with an ankle injury. Head coach Dan Campbell said that it will cause the star receiver to miss practice on Wednesday before their Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell added that he anticipates St. Brown returning on Thursday, but his status is unknown right now. He noted that St. Brown, along with Ennis Rakestraw, are still expected to play this week, but he was not definitive. "I think, like, he and Ennis, I think those guys will probably sit Wednesday," said Campbell. but the plan is to get them going Thursday, and I think they'll be fine; they should be good. Now, we will see when we get there." Detroit Lions Wide Receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown Has Ankle Injury Before Week 8 St. Brown played 53 snaps in the Lions' Week 7 win. It amounted to 77.9% of the snaps. That is the second-lowest rate of the season. He played 48 snaps, amounting to 74% of the snaps earlier in the year. St. Brown had a good start to his 2026 season, but it was not quite on par with other seasons, or the progression he was hoping to show. The All-Pro receiver noted that he was playing decent prior to the Packers game. "Five games into the year, I feel like I've been playing decent ball," St. Brown said when asked to describe his play. He responded with his best game of the season. St. Brown produced nine receptions for 153 yards in the Lions win. He produced nine catches for 142 yards against the Buffalo Bills in Week 2, but that was in a loss. The big impact in a winning performance made it a clear-cut best game of his season. home.headline: Lions, Packers Week 7 injury report: Bye week helps Detroit get healthy
home.blurb: C Cade Mays (Wrist, PUP) — Will return to the active roster this week S Brian Branch (Achilles, PUP) — Will return to the active roster this week On Monday, coach Dan Campbell told the media that the plan was to activate both Mays and Branch to the 53-man roster this week, but it was unclear how much either could play against the Packers. Branch is expected to “handle quite a bit,” but he may not be able to play the entire game, while Mays is expected to start based on Campbell’s comments on Wednesday : “We really worked the heck out of Cade yesterday. He got some quality reps, and we would like to give him a go here.” RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December S Kerby Joseph (Knee, PUP) — expected to return to play this season Branch’s safety running mate, Kerby Joseph, also got some positive news this week, as Campbell noted on Tuesday that he still expects the All-Pro safety to return to play this season. While there is still no timetable for his return, this was the first positive update we have gotten from coaches surrounding Joseph’s status and was quickly followed up by even more promising videos posted on Joseph’s social media accounts . Ya-Sin was injured on special teams in Week 4, missed the Lions game in Week 5, but was able to get healthy enough to practice over the bye and was back on the practice field on Tuesday. While he’s no longer in the starting lineup on defense, he’s been a steady contributor on multiple phases of special teams and would boost multiple spots if he could return to game action. C Cade Mays (Wrist) — Upgraded from limited practice S Brian Branch (Achilles) — Upgraded from limited practice As mentioned above, Mays and Branch are on track to return and start this week. Williams was limited in practice in Week 5 but was able to play a full complement of snaps in the game and looked like the injury didn’t limit him. Wonnum also managed to play in Week 5 (50% of defensive snaps), but it’s unclear if his snaps were scaled back a tick due to injury or schematic approach. It didn’t look like his injury limited him too much, considering he registered another two sacks in the game. home.headline: Detroit Lions Injury Report for Thursday, October 22
home.blurb: Defensive back Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were both full participants in Thursday's practice, while cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) remained limited. The report marks another positive step for Branch and Mays, who are both expected to return to action Sunday at Ford Field. Wednesday's participation designations were estimates because the Lions did not practice. Injury report key: FP = Full Participation; LP = Limited Participation. As we previously reported when Dan Campbell discussed Branch's return , the Lions expect their talented defensive back to contribute against Green Bay, although his workload could be monitored following his lengthy recovery from a torn Achilles. The veteran cornerback was also listed as limited Wednesday, meaning his designation remains unchanged heading into the final practice of the week. The good news is that all three players listed on Detroit's injury report were able to participate in Thursday's practice at some level. A review of the Lions' Thursday injury situation also highlights the team's improving health coming out of its bye week. With Branch and Mays practicing fully and Ya-Sin remaining involved on a limited basis, Detroit appears to be making progress at an important point in the season. The Lions will release their final injury report Friday, providing a clearer picture of who will be available for Sunday's showdown against the Packers. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells Mon, October 26, 2026 at 2:27 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their second straight game against an AFC East opponent on Sunday. Last week the Jets lost a hard fought game to the defending AFC champions New England Patriots. That was understandable. Much less understandable was today's 28 – 25 loss at home to the previously winless Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins dominated the action for most of the game, building a two touchdown lead at halftime and maintaining an 11 point lead with less than five minutes remaining in the game before a late Jets touchdown made the score look closer than the game actually was. This loss came against a Dolphins team that had never held a lead at any point in the season prior to today. Today the Dolphins never trailed. It was a humiliating performance by the Jets. The horrendous Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-5 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Now the Jets look to get back on the winning track as they stay home to take on the 3-4 Las Vegas Raiders in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Raiders have lost four straight games after starting the season 3-0. Their latest loss came at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams by a 35 – 21 score. The Raiders' defense has collapsed in their four game losing streak, surrendering 30+ points in each of the four games. With the Raiders making the long trip east for this game and suffering through the early game start, on paper this looks like a get well game for the Jets. However, the way the Jets are playing no game on the schedule should be looked at as an easy win. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think this game is close to a tossup. The current line has the Jets home favorites by 1.5 points. The game has an over/under of 44.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are -118 while the Dolphins are +100. Let's see if the Jets can recover from a terrible loss and take care of business at home against the Raiders. J-E-T-S!
