The Las Vegas Raiders travel to MetLife Stadium for a Week 8 showdown against the New York Jets. Scheduled for Sunday, November 1, 2026, at 1:00 PM, this game will be broadcast on FOX. The Raiders, hailing from the AFC West, will face the AFC East's Jets in what promises to be a compelling game. Klint Kubiak leads the Raiders as head coach, with Andrew Janocko and Rob Leonard serving as the offensive and defensive coordinators, respectively. With a current record of 3-4, the Raiders have shown strength on the road, boasting a 2-1 away record. However, they are coming off a recent home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, 35-21. The New York Jets, under head coach Aaron Glenn, have struggled this season, holding a 2-5 record. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich and defensive coordinator Brian Duker will look to turn things around at home. The Jets recently suffered a close defeat to the Miami Dolphins, losing 28-25 at MetLife Stadium. In terms of betting odds, the Jets are slight favorites with a moneyline of -122 compared to the Raiders' +102. The spread is tight, with the Jets at -1.5 and the Raiders at +1.5, while the total is set at 45.5 points. Both teams will be eager to secure a win to improve their standings as the season progresses. Jets vs Raiders At a Glance (Week 8) The game is scheduled for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL Regular Season. The Las Vegas Raiders have a current record of 3-4-0. The New York Jets hold a record of 2-5-0. The game will be held at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. The Jets are slight favorites with a moneyline of -122. The total points over/under is set at 45.5. Jets Ready to Soar: New York Jets Home Game Preview Offensive Overview The New York Jets' offense in the 2026 regular season has shown mixed results, ranking 20th overall in offensive yards with 2,121 yards. Their average of 19.6 points per game places them 23rd in the league, indicating room for improvement in scoring efficiency. Quarterback Geno Smith has been a key figure, amassing 1,623 passing yards and 10 touchdowns in seven games. However, the rushing attack has struggled, ranking 21st with 675 total rushing yards this season. Defensive Strengths Defensively, the Jets have been more consistent, ranking 12th in opponent scoring with an average of 21.4 points allowed per game. Their pass defense is particularly strong, allowing only 187.7 passing yards per game, ranking 5th in the league. The Jets' ability to pressure the quarterback has been impressive, with 19 sacks ranking them 3rd in the league. This defensive pressure could be pivotal in their upcoming game against the Raiders. Injury Concerns The Jets face several injury challenges, notably with running back Breece Hall listed as questionable with a quad injury. Additionally, the defensive line is affected with David Onyemata and Tre Brown on the injured reserve list. The offensive line also has concerns, with Dylan Parham and Max Mitchell questionable for the upcoming game. Managing these injuries will be crucial for the Jets' success. Key Players to Watch Geno Smith remains a focal point, leading the team with his passing prowess. His connection with wide receiver Garrett Wilson, who has 444 receiving yards, will be essential in the passing game. On defense, Minkah Fitzpatrick has been a standout, contributing significantly to the secondary's strong performance. His playmaking ability could disrupt the Raiders' passing attack. Recent Game Recap In their last game, the Jets narrowly lost to the Miami Dolphins 28-25 at home. The offense showed potential with 269 passing yards, but the defense struggled to contain the Dolphins' rushing attack. Geno Smith's performance was commendable, throwing for 287 yards and three touchdowns. However, the Jets must address their rushing defense to improve their chances against the Raiders. Team Betting Trends The Jets have gone over the total in 63.6% of their last 11 games as underdogs. Overall, the over has hit in 61.5% of the Jets' last 13 games. In home games, the over is 4-2 in the last six outings. After a loss, the Jets have covered the spread in only 36.4% of their last 11 games. As underdogs, they have struggled with a 25% ATS record in the last 12 games. Las Vegas Raiders Prepare for Showdown Against the New York Jets Offensive Powerhouse The Las Vegas Raiders have been a strong offensive unit this season, scoring 183 points and ranking 4th in the league. With an average of 26.1 points per game, they sit 7th in this category. Their passing attack has been particularly potent, recording 1883 passing yards, which is the 2nd highest in the league. Kirk Cousins has been instrumental in the Raiders' aerial success, throwing for 1877 yards with 16 touchdowns, leading the league in passing touchdowns. Tre Tucker has emerged as a key target with 474 receiving yards and 4 touchdowns, ranking 16th in the league for receiving yards. Tight end Brock Bowers has also been a critical piece, with 455 receiving yards and 3 touchdowns. Defensive Challenges While the Raiders' offense has been thriving, their defense has faced its share of challenges. They have allowed 197 points, ranking them 28th in points allowed. Their run defense has been particularly vulnerable, giving up 1005 rushing yards, the 31st in the league. However, the Raiders' pass rush has been effective, with 16 sacks placing them 6th in the league. The team has also excelled in takeaways, ranking 2nd with 12 takeaways, indicating their ability to capitalize on opponents' mistakes. Recent Performance Insights In their recent games, the Raiders have experienced a mixed bag of outcomes, holding a 3-4 record. Despite a tough loss to the Rams, where they allowed 35 points, the team showcased offensive prowess with 302 passing yards. The game against the Bills was another close encounter, ending 33-30, with Cousins throwing for 313 yards and 2 touchdowns. Defense remains a concern, as seen in their 45-17 loss to the Patriots, where they struggled to contain the opponent's offense. However, their victory over the Saints, 35-27, highlighted their offensive capabilities, with Cousins throwing for 3 touchdowns. As the Raiders head into their matchup against the New York Jets, Kirk Cousins will be a focal point, leading the offense with precision. Ashton Jeanty, the team's leading rusher with 328 yards, will be crucial in establishing a ground game. On the receiving end, Tre Tucker and Brock Bowers will aim to exploit the Jets' secondary. Defensively, Maxx Crosby will look to disrupt the Jets' offensive line, contributing to the Raiders' pass-rushing efforts. Nakobe Dean's playmaking abilities will be pivotal in anchoring the defense and providing leadership on the field. Betting Trends The Raiders have hit the over in their last 5 games, making them 5-0 on the over in 2026. As underdogs, they have also seen the total go over in their last 5 games this season. With the Raiders' potent offense averaging 26.1 points per game, the total score is likely to exceed expectations. Las Vegas Raiders' games have frequently gone over the total due to their high-scoring offense and struggling defense, which ranks 26th in points allowed per game. Playing on the road, they've managed a 2-1 record, showing their ability to score effectively away from home. This dynamic further supports the likelihood of a high-scoring game. Head-to-head, the previous meetings between these two teams have seen significant scoring, such as the 31-28 outcome at MetLife Stadium in 2020. With both teams showing vulnerabilities on defense and capability on offense, a similar high total seems plausible. The combination of both teams' defensive weaknesses and offensive strengths suggests a game surpassing 45.5 points. Getty Cole Sullivan Thu, October 22, 2026 at 9:02 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The New York Jets are 2-4 entering Sunday's Week 7 contest against AFC East rival Miami Dolphins. Ahead of the matchup, the Jets are dealing with several injuries, and the most notable is running back Breece Hall. He has been sidelined with a quadriceps/groin injury since Week 3, when he left the team's matchup against the Detroit Lions in the fourth quarter. Hall appeared on the practice field wearing his helmet and stretched with the team, which is an encouraging sign for his progress. New York Post Jets beat reporter Brian Costello reported that Hall eventually headed to the rehab area as reporters left practice, indicating he likely wouldn't participate in team drills. Still, his appearance on the field marks a step in the right direction. "Breece Hall is moving well at practice. I'd be optimistic about him playing. We'll know more tomorrow," Costello posted on X. With Hall sidelined, Braelon Allen has stepped into the Jets' starting running back role and has been productive as the primary back. Allen had 17 carries for 78 yards and two receptions for 26 yards last week against the New England Patriots . The week before, he logged 24 carries for 116 yards and a touchdown. However, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn made it clear that Hall will reclaim the starting job when he returns, though Allen will remain a focal point of the offense. "Breece is our starter, he's always been our starter, but Braelon is going to get touches," Glenn said earlier this week. picks.blurb: Week 8 odds: The Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rays rally, avoid sweep Anthony Edwards injury NFL Power Rankings WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Jayson Tatum buzzer-beater Week 8 odds: The Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Browns (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jason Aponte Tue, October 27, 2026 at 4:54 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers have a chance to take over first place in the AFC North with a win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. This is the second meeting between the division rivals, with Pittsburgh looking to avenge a loss from the first meeting. The first meeting went down to the wire in Cleveland, and things are different for both teams ahead of the second matchup. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open up as 3.5 point favorites at home. Vegas believes the game will be a defensive struggle, with the over/under set at 39.5. The Steelers moneyline is set at -198. The Browns have won two straight over Pittsburgh, but both matchups were in Cleveland. Each game was won by one possession. The last regular-season win in Pittsburgh for the Browns happened in 2003. However, the biggest win came in 2020 in the AFC Wild Card round, with Baker Mayfield and the Browns prevailing 48-37. In fact, the 2003 victory is the only regular-season win for Cleveland at Acrisure Stadium. The Steelers have won 12 straight at home against Cleveland, but have dropped five straight in Cleveland. The rivalry is still in Pittsburgh's favor with an 83-66-1 record over the Browns. The Steelers' run defense will have to remain stingy as Quinshon Judkins returned from injury last week and went over 100 rushing yards against Tennessee. The run defense is the seventh-best in the NFL, allowing 91 rushing yards per game and four rushing touchdowns on the season. Meanwhile, the Browns run defense is vulnerable with 116.4 rushing yards allowed per game and four touchdowns allowed. Sticking with the hot hand of Jaylen Warren should be the game plan for Pittsburgh. Rico Dowdle has been involved, and it's clear Mike McCarthy wants to get back to a rotation at running back. With the wide receiver injuries, expect both to be on the field at the same time. Let us know what you think in the comments . away.blurb: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return Skip to main content SI.COM The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans came out. Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville. Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver. Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers. However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game. The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week. The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since. The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games. Michael Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Out Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game. Dillon Gabriel, Teven Jenkins, Out Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line. If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2. The Titans do not have much to offer on offense, but rookie Carnell Tate is having a solid season with 344 yards, which is only one yard behind Denzel Boston. Todd Monken believes that Ward will play with a finger injury, but advised, “We’ll see”. When Ward is on the field, quarterbacks generally do not even try to throw his way, but quarterback Cameron Ward can be reckless with the football and throw it his way, leading to a crucial turnover. home.headline: Steelers' TJ Watt pops up on injury report with new concern
home.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. Related Articles Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t been able to catch a break from injuries the last few weeks. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. home.headline: Steelers Injury Situation Finally Trending in Right Direction
home.blurb: Thakfully, those scares didn't continue after the game. Watt made it through unscathed, as did the rest of the lineup. Head coach Mike McCarthy confirmed in his weekly press conference that there were no other major injuries coming out of their international meeting. The team also had one of their most positive injury developments in Week 7. Safety DeShon Elliott returned after almost a year due to a lower-body injury. He played in a limited number of snaps, but it was huge to get the star safety back in any capacity. Wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. may also return this season, but reports from Pat McAfee Show corospondent Mark Kaboly say there's a chance Pittman Jr. misses the rest of the year. For head coach Mike McCarthy, things are finally coming together. In his mind, the roster is in great shape. As they wait for a few pieces to return, McCarthy is confident that their mix of players gives the Steelers what they need for a run in 2026. And it's all coming together without critical pieces like Wilson and Harmon. Add in veterans Michael Pittman Jr. and Sebastian Joseph-Day and their unknown return timelines, and this team is trending in the right direction health-wise at the perfect time. PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are finally trending in the right direction in more ways than one. The team won their fifth game of the season, taking down the New Orleans Saints in an international contest. Now, the Steelers turn their focus to the Cleveland Browns in Week 8. The goal is to capture their sixth victory and even the season series against the Browns. In that Week 8 contest, the Steelers will play a bit shorthanded. With multiple key players on the Injured Reserve, the team will have to dig deep to find that win. Thankfully, the team is improving week after week, and the schedule is only helping this team navigate their early-season injury troubles. The Steelers had plenty of injury scares heading to Paris, France, for their Week 7 battle. A day before their flight departed, edge rusher T.J. Watt popped up on the team's injury report with a calf ailment. He was just the latest of multiple players dealing with various ailments of different severities. It was exactly what the Steelers needed. The good news for the Steelers is that the schedule has been on their side. Over the past few weeks, the regular season schedule has been quite favorable for Pittsburgh. Taking on opponents like the Indianapolis Colts, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the New Orleans Saints, a trio of inferior competition allowed the Steelers to easily weather the storm of injuries. Following this Week 8 game, the Steelers will walk into their bye week. It comes at a sorely needed time, with players like wide receiver Roman Wilson and defensive tackle Derrick Harmon nearing the end of the four required games missed on IR. away.headline: Kendal Daniels goes from being carted off field to saving Falcons’ season
away.blurb: Kendal Daniels goes from being carted off field to saving Falcons’ season | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services Apple TV Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels experienced one of the most remarkable turnarounds of the NFL season, going from being carted off the field on a stretcher to delivering a game-changing performance just seven days later. Daniels recorded 11 tackles, an interception and a fumble recovery in Atlanta’s 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The victory improved Atlanta’s record to 3-4 while handing San Francisco its first loss of the season. Just one week earlier, Daniels suffered a frightening neck injury against the Chicago Bears that required medical personnel to immobilize him before transporting him to Grady Hospital. However, the rookie returned to practice Wednesday and was cleared to play against San Francisco. “It’s been the craziest week of my life,” Daniels told ESPN . “I’ve never not walked off the field after an injury.” Daniels delivered his biggest play with Atlanta protecting a 26-20 fourth-quarter lead. With approximately three minutes remaining, Daniels intercepted quarterback Brock Purdy and returned the football 29 yards, setting up Nick Folk’s 31-yard field goal. He later recovered a fumble forced by safety Jessie Bates III, officially ending San Francisco’s comeback hopes. Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski praised the rookie’s resilience following the victory. “That’s remarkable, truly,” Stefanski said. “What a great kid. We just gave him a game ball, and he deserves it because what a week.” Daniels also handled defensive communication responsibilities with veteran linebacker Divine Deablo sidelined by a forearm injury. His performance highlighted an Atlanta defense that forced four turnovers against one of the NFL’s strongest teams. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. contributed three touchdown passes and 213 passing yards in the victory. For Atlanta, the win snapped a two-game losing streak and provided much-needed momentum heading into an important NFC South matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . For Daniels, Sunday’s performance represented something even greater: an inspiring comeback that his teammates will remember throughout the season. away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts announced several roster moves at the cornerback position. Cam Taylor-Britt exited Sunday's game against Minnesota with a groin injury, and he has been placed on injured reserve. Taking his spot on the active roster is Kenneth Harris, who was signed from the practice squad. Harris was elevated for Sunday's game and ended up playing 17 defensive snaps due to injuries. He allowed no receptions on two targets and forced a pass breakup, according to Pro Football Focus. Sauce Gardner did not play on Sunday due to a calf injury, while Justin Walley exited the game with an injury. Depending on the availability of these two players this week, the Colts may have to turn to Harris again. The Colts also signed cornerbacks Shemar Bartholomew and Natrone Brooks to the practice squad. Bartholomew went undrafted in 2024 and has played 51 career defensive snaps. Brooks went undrafted in 2023 and has played 118 career snaps. This article originally appeared on Colts Wire: Colts make several roster moves at CB while navigating injuries

Colts head coach Shane Steichen on Friday ruled out wide receiver Anthony Gould (concussion), tight end Tyler Warren (groin) and cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. home.headline: Vega Ioane's injury could give Jaguars' D-line a sudden edge against Ravens
home.blurb: Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Ioane suffered an MCL sprain, adding that he'll miss time even though it's a short-term injury. The rookie hog molly left the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and didn't return. It's hard to tell just how much time is a little time, but if it wasn't serious, Ioane would be week-to-week or questionable for Week 8. He's not, meaning that there's a strong chance he won't suit up against Jacksonville. Following their BYE, the Jacksonville Jaguars will face the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8 . And after their AFC showdown, they'll face off against the Baltimore Ravens. While it's hard to tell if Lamar Jackson will suit up for the game — he's seemingly dealing with a high-ankle sprain — the Jags now know that they probably won't have to face rookie offensive guard Vega Ioane. The Jaguars may not have to worry about Vega Ioane when they play the Ravens The Jaguars will face Baltimore in Week 9. It will be a Thursday Night game. Given that there's a three-day gap between Sunday games and Thursday, players who don't suit up Sunday often miss the Thursday bout. That doesn't bode well for Vega Ioane's availability. A first-round pick of the Ravens in 2026, Ioane got off to a strong start to his rookie season, giving up just one sack and eight total pressures in six games. Ioane began the season at right guard but eventually moved to center. He returned to right guard when Baltimore traded for Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles. Emery Jones Jr. may be the next man up. You may also like: AFC South Week 8 power ranking: The Jags win big without playing The Jaguars' D-Line must take advantage of Vega Ioane's absence Lamar Jackson has missed three games with injuries . Tyler Huntley has filled in for him, throwing for 664 yards with four touchdowns and one interception during his absence. There hasn't been that steep a drop-off at quarterback, but without Vega Ioane, the Baltimore offensive line could have trouble protecting whoever lines up behind center. This is encouraging news for a Jacksonville defensive line that has struggled to create pressure from the interior. While the Jaguars excel at stuffing the run, they have had trouble getting after the quarterback this season, registering just 11 sacks. Sure, they've racked up pressures, but those haven't always translated into big plays, takeaways, and such. Maybe the Jags can get better production from their interior defensive line after their break. Arik Armstead has played at a high level at times but has been inconsistent. On the other hand, DaVon Hamilton won't offer much in the pass-rush department, while Ruke Orhorhoro hasn't made the leap he was expected to make when he was traded to Jacksonville. Rookie Albert Regis is also in the mix but has barely played. When you add it all up, it's easy to see why the Jaguars are being urged to trade for a defensive tackle . Maybe they will, maybe they won't, but they'll at least get a bit of a break when they play the Rave

home.headline: Jaguars' Power Rankings Roundup Has Jacksonville Anywhere From No. 2 to No. 9 After the Bye
home.blurb: Sitting out Week 7 turned out to be a pretty good week for the Jacksonville Jaguars. With the Texans and Colts both losing, they won the bye week in the AFC South, and the national power rankings mostly kept them right where they were. Mostly is the key word. One outlet vaulted Jacksonville all the way to No. 2, while two others nudged it down a spot. The Colts come to town Sunday, and CBS isn’t sure yet how much the Anton Harrison injury changes things. PFT is the high outlet by a mile. It moved Jacksonville up two spots without a game and poked a little fun at itself in the process. “For the first time ever, a team ascends to No. 2 without playing,” PFT wrote in its rankings , using the same line it gave the No. 1 Bills. ESPN’s panel dropped the Jaguars one spot as Seattle moved past them. This week’s list named each team’s best offseason addition, and Michael DiRocco went with rookie left guard Emmanuel Pregnon, a third-round pick who earned first-team reps when injuries shuffled the line in camp. The impact shows up in short yardage. DiRocco wrote for ESPN that the Jaguars averaged 1.3 yards per carry on third-and-short in 2025, last in the league, and are at 3.1 this year, eighth-best. That was a priority for Liam Coen. Ralph Vacchiano held Jacksonville at No. 8 but sounded ready to move it up. He called the 34 points the defense allowed to Houston before the bye “a real anomaly” and pointed to a schedule with the Colts, Ravens, Giants and Titans twice over the next five weeks. “The Jaguars could be rising in these rankings fast,” Vacchiano wrote for FOX Sports . FOX also noted the Jaguars have gone 23 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher, tied for the third-longest streak since 1966. That’s part of why the division looks like an easy path to the playoffs right now. Pete Prisco dropped Jacksonville a spot and focused on the left tackle spot. “They come off their bye with the news that left tackle Anton Harrison is done for the year with a knee injury,” Prisco wrote for CBS Sports . “Walker Little played well against the Texans, but can he hold up?” The Jaguars are turning to Walker Little for the rest of the year, and the Colts are his first test. The pass rush has its own fixes to make on the other side of the ball. Averaged across the four outlets, Jacksonville sits at about No. 6, the same as a week ago. The range runs from No. 2 to No. 9, which tells you the national view hasn’t settled. A win over Indianapolis wouldn’t settle it either, but it would keep the Jaguars in control of the AFC South . home.blurb: Return Of The 'X-Factor': Brian Branch Makes Lions A Legit Super Bowl Contender my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores National Football League Add FOX Sports on Google Jaguars Get Devastating Injury Update On Left Tackle Anton Harrison Published Oct. 23, 2026 1:01 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the remainder of the season after tearing a ligament in his right knee. Harrison injured his knee during a win against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Oct. 11. He spun on the field turf to make a block and twisted his knee when he planted his right leg. Harrison was carted to the locker room. Harrison waited until the Jaguars (4-2) returned from two weeks overseas to have arthroscopic surgery to determine the extent of the damage. The scope Wednesday revealed a torn anterior cruciate ligament. Jacksonville already placed Harrison on injured reserve. Backup Walker Little, who has started 40 games over six seasons with Jacksonville, is expected to replace Harrison in the lineup the rest of the season. Harrison has started 53 games for the Jaguars since they selected him 27th overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. The former Oklahoma Sooners standout moved from right tackle to left tackle this season in hopes of improving Jacksonville’s run game, which ranks 14th this season, up from 20th in 2025. Harrison is Jacksonville's first starter to sustain a season-ending injury in 2026. Reporting by The Associated Press. home.headline: Updating Every Key Jaguars Injury Entering Bye Week: From Anton Harrison to Montaric Brown
home.blurb: Sitting at 4-2 entering Week 7, the Jaguars have a number of injuries that the bye week could aid in terms of getting players back to full speed. So, who is injured and who could return? Jaguars cornerback Montaric Brown has had a 2026 to forget so far. After giving up a few explosive plays during the first two games, Brown sustained a hamstring injury in Week 3 that has since limited him. He missed the Week 4 game due to the injury, played just six snaps in Week 5 the following week, and then did not play last week against the Houston Texans. and part of it has to do with injuries to Brown and others. The fact he hasn’t been put on IR is a good sign, and he might’ve needed the bye week more than anyone else on the roster. His status post-bye will be revealed likely next week. Jaguars’ second-year safety Caleb Ransaw went down with a knee injury in Week 4 and has missed the last two games as a result, which has led to a depth issue at the safety position. It remains to be seen what an actual timetable will look like for Ransaw, with Jaguars head coach Liam Coen giving a “no comment” reply when asked if Ransaw would be out for the season following his injury. Ransaw has missed a ton of time with injuries in his NFL career and has been on IR over the last two weeks. We will likely not know if Ransaw will return until later in the season, but the Jaguars have some legit safety depth issues behind him. The Jaguars’ big fish in free agency last season, Patrick Mekari has not played a snap this year due to a back injury that also kept him out of training camp. Coen did note this week, however, that Mekari is the closest person to returning of the multiple players the Jaguars have on IR. Whether that means he plays or just serves as depth remains to be seen, though the latter seems significantly more likely. “Mekari [OL Patrick Mekari] could obviously be somebody from a depth standpoint that can be available for us to be able to help us as we go, for sure. But I wouldn't see anybody else at the moment,” Coen said. The Jaguars’ second-year defensive end has been on injured reserve since sustaining an upper-body injury during the first week of the season. He had a stellar training camp and could help the Jaguars get more pressure on the quarterback once he is back to 100%, with Coen noting that he is the second-closest player ready to return after Mekari. News Sports Entertainment Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS Anton Harrison injury update: Jaguars OL reportedly to miss rest of year Juston Lewis Jacksonville Florida Times-Union Updated Oct. 23, 2026, 10:49 a.m. ET Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the rest of the season with a torn ACL. The injury was discovered to be more severe than initially thought during a recent procedure. Walker Little is expected to replace Harrison as the starting left tackle. The Jacksonville Jaguars will reportedly be without left tackle Anton Harrison for the remainder of the season, per NFL Media's Ian Rapoport . Harrison, who was placed on injured reserve last week after suffering a knee injury against the Philadelphia Eagles in London, suffered a torn ACL and will be sidelined for the duration of the season. Doctors found more damage than initially believed during a procedure on Oct. 22, thus leaving the Jaguars without their top blindside protector. The team exercised the fifth-year option on Harrison in April, which ties him to the club through the 2027 season. The former first-rounder was playing his first season at left tackle in the NFL after winning the job in training camp. He stepped in for the injured Cole Van Lanen , who's 2025 season ended after a knee injury sidelined him last year. Van Lanen started training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list, working to the side as he rehabbed for a majority of the preseason. He returned to the field as Jacksonville's right tackle, with Harrison winning the job of protecting Trevor Lawrence's back. Walker Little will fill in for Harrison for the remainder of the season as he did last week against the Houston Texans . He's one of the most tenured linemen for the Jaguars and has appeared in 76 games for Jacksonville with 40 starts. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. The Chargers are 0-6 and playing for pride, while the Rams need a win to keep their playoff hopes on track, even without WR Davante Adams and Myles Garrett. You can see all of our NFL picks for Week 8 , but here’s why I’m backing the Rams to cover, and how you can bet on Chargers vs Rams. Sunday, Nov 1 · 4:05 PM ET · SoFi Stadium · FOX Chargers vs Rams Betting Odds (BetUS) Los Angeles Chargers The Chargers have the worst record in the NFL at 0-6, and the offense is the biggest problem. They’re scoring just 15 points per game, the fewest in the league, and Justin Herbert has been under constant pressure behind a line that has allowed 21 sacks, the most per game in the NFL. Los Angeles Rams The Rams are dealing with major injuries, but their offense is still the most productive in the league at 399.1 yards per game. Turnovers and red-zone finishing have held them back at times, but Matthew Stafford keeps delivering, and apart from the season opener against the 49ers in Melbourne and the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, they’ve scored 20 or more points in every game. RB Kyren Williams is also in excellent form and regularly tops 100 scrimmage yards, which makes him one to watch in the NFL player props market this week. Stafford has far better protection than Herbert, who has taken too many hits through six games, and the Chargers struggle to even get into scoring position. That gap is the biggest reason we’re backing the Rams to cover. With both teams sharing SoFi Stadium, there’s little true home-field advantage here, so this comes down to quality, and the Rams have far more of it. It’s a lot of points to lay, but against an offense averaging 15 points per game, the Rams can get there. The over looks like the play on the total. The Rams lead the NFL with 399.1 yards per game and have topped 20 points in all but two games, and with Kyren Williams in excellent form, they can do most of the heavy lifting here. away.blurb: While it has been an odd season filled with surprises, one thing has been unsurprising: injuries piling up for players in the Powder Blue uniform. Injuries always seem to happen for the Chargers, an unfortunate certainty fans can count on year in and year out. Alt has officially returned to practice today, Oct. 21, the Chargers' first practice since losing to the Chiefs. Along with his return, the Chargers' starting left guard, Kayode Awosika , has also returned to practice after missing time with his fibula injury. He missed a total of four games. Now that the Chargers are back with two more of their offensive linemen, the offensive line will once again be shuffled to ensure the "best 5" are out in front of Justin Herbert. With rookies Travis Burke, Logan Taylor and Alex Harkey all being starters over the last two weeks, who will be the rookies to be replaced first? The only step left for the Bolts is to see Rashawn Slater return from injured reserve and get this offensive line back to health. They have dealt with injuries, poor play from multiple units and extremely poor coaching from coaches who seemingly have never had a track record of being bad. One of the biggest injuries suffered thus far in the 2026 NFL season has been Pro Bowl offensive tackle, former Top 5 selection, Joe Alt. Alt suffered a neck injury against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4 due to a freak helicopter-esque kick from Seahawks defender Nick Emmanwori. The play where Joe Alt is injured by Seahawks DB Nick Emmanwori pic.twitter.com/2P0KMGTzAl Cannot exactly say I have seen anything like that happen in an NFL game, but also I cannot say I thought the Chargers were going to be 0-6 to start this NFL season either. Moving on, Alt has missed two games: the Chargers' losses to the Denver Broncos and the Kansas City Chiefs. Anytime you are dealing with a neck injury, it is important to prioritize safety over rushing back, allowing Alt to spend time with a specialist and get clearance to begin practicing on Oct. 18. RT Joe Alt (neck) and LG Kayode Awosika (fibula) were participating during the portion of today’s Chargers practice open to the media. Who is the Starting 5 OL for the Chargers After the Bye Week? home.headline: Rams' Power Rankings Roundup Has Los Angeles Rising Everywhere as the Run Game Returns
home.blurb: Ralph Vacchiano gave the Rams the biggest jump, four spots, and opened his blurb with a movie line. “Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in,” he wrote for FOX Sports , crediting Matthew Stafford’s passing and the “two-pronged rushing attack” of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. McDuffie has missed the last two games with a groin injury, but Barshop wrote for ESPN that he’s allowed a 28.6% completion rate in coverage, the best of any player targeted at least 20 times, according to Next Gen Stats. Even with him out, the Rams have stayed top 12 on both sides of the ball by EPA per play. Building a 28-3 lead in Las Vegas was the kind of performance the Los Angeles Rams needed, and the national power rankings noticed. All four major outlets moved the Rams up after their 35-21 win over the Raiders , and two of them pushed L.A. into the top 12. The common thread was the run game. Three of the four write-ups mentioned it, and at 3-4, it might be what decides whether this is a turnaround or another one-week spike. He’s not all the way in. “If only they could put it together for more than one game at a time,” Vacchiano wrote. FOX also noted Stafford’s three touchdown passes made him the franchise leader, a record he joked about after the game . ESPN’s panel moved L.A. up two spots. This week’s list named each team’s best offseason addition, and Sarah Barshop chose cornerback Trent McDuffie, whom the Rams acquired in a trade and made the highest-paid corner in league history at the time. Pete Prisco moved the Rams up two spots and sounded like he’d been waiting for this version all year. “The team we saw beat up the Raiders is the Dream Team we expected to see before the season. The run game is back,” Prisco wrote for CBS Sports . PFT only bumped L.A. a spot, but it landed in the same place. “If they can keep running the ball the way they did on Sunday, they can start stacking wins,” PFT wrote in its rankings . Averaged across the four outlets, the Rams sit at about No. 14, up from roughly No. 16 a week ago. That’s a solid climb for one win, and the winless Chargers come to SoFi Stadium on Sunday. Every Rams loss also helps Cleveland , which owns their 2027 first, so stacking wins matters for more than just the standings. away.blurb: “We’re trying to get him touches. He’s one of our explosive playmakers," Payton told reporters via conference call on Monday. "Quite honestly, we need to get him more touches on offense, and we’ll do that. A lot of it had to do with the way they were kicking off. We kind of, you noticed, went more to a single returner and certainly that first one (return) that puts us at midfield was a big one for us.” The Denver Broncos made a pair of roster moves in the lead-up to their Week 8 home showdown with the Kansas City Chiefs. The team announced Tuesday that it has signed wide receiver Eli Pancol to the practice squad. In a corresponding transaction, Denver released defensive back Ugo Amadi — who joined the club on Oct. 9 — from the taxi squad. Undrafted in 2025 and yet to appear in an NFL game, Pancol spent his rookie campaign with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Indianapolis Colts, with whom he signed a reserve/future contract in January. The Colts waived him at final cuts and eventually released him again last week following a second stint on the practice squad. Due to injuries, the 6-foot-3, 205-pound wideout was a five-year collegiate contributor at Duke, catching 130 passes for 1,710 yards and 14 touchdowns from 2019-2024. He added seven rushes for 40 yards and two scores on the ground. In 2024, he earned third-team All-ACC honors while taking home the Brian Piccolo Award, given to the “most courageous” football player in the Atlantic Coast Conference. Pancol ran a 4.40 forty-yard dash and recorded a 36-inch vertical jump at his Pro Day prior to turning pro. "Any team that gets Eli Pancol is getting a relentless hard worker," Pancol told The Draft Network in a 2025 interview. "I’ve proven that no matter how much adversity comes my way, I’m always going to overcome the obstacles. I’m coming to work every single day to get better. I love the game of football. I love feeding off the energy of the fans. I use that to energize my teammates. I’m also a physical receiver who loves to block. I’m ready to work. You can’t go wrong with somebody like me." Interestingly, Pancol becomes the fifth WR to land on Denver's practice squad, joining the likes of Dane Key, Cameron Ross, Kolbe Katsis, and Michael Bandy. None of these incumbents have been promoted to the active roster in recent weeks. Speaking of the 53, the Broncos could be a little shorthanded at the position in Week 8 with Pat Bryant still on short-term injured reserve and Jaylen Waddle emerging from Sunday's win over the Cardinals with an apparent chest issue. home.headline: Broncos Add WR to Practice Squad Ahead of Week 8 vs. Chiefs
home.blurb: “We’re trying to get him touches. He’s one of our explosive playmakers," Payton told reporters via conference call on Monday. "Quite honestly, we need to get him more touches on offense, and we’ll do that. A lot of it had to do with the way they were kicking off. We kind of, you noticed, went more to a single returner and certainly that first one (return) that puts us at midfield was a big one for us.” The Denver Broncos made a pair of roster moves in the lead-up to their Week 8 home showdown with the Kansas City Chiefs. The team announced Tuesday that it has signed wide receiver Eli Pancol to the practice squad. In a corresponding transaction, Denver released defensive back Ugo Amadi — who joined the club on Oct. 9 — from the taxi squad. Undrafted in 2025 and yet to appear in an NFL game, Pancol spent his rookie campaign with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Indianapolis Colts, with whom he signed a reserve/future contract in January. The Colts waived him at final cuts and eventually released him again last week following a second stint on the practice squad. Due to injuries, the 6-foot-3, 205-pound wideout was a five-year collegiate contributor at Duke, catching 130 passes for 1,710 yards and 14 touchdowns from 2019-2024. He added seven rushes for 40 yards and two scores on the ground. In 2024, he earned third-team All-ACC honors while taking home the Brian Piccolo Award, given to the “most courageous” football player in the Atlantic Coast Conference. Pancol ran a 4.40 forty-yard dash and recorded a 36-inch vertical jump at his Pro Day prior to turning pro. "Any team that gets Eli Pancol is getting a relentless hard worker," Pancol told The Draft Network in a 2025 interview. "I’ve proven that no matter how much adversity comes my way, I’m always going to overcome the obstacles. I’m coming to work every single day to get better. I love the game of football. I love feeding off the energy of the fans. I use that to energize my teammates. I’m also a physical receiver who loves to block. I’m ready to work. You can’t go wrong with somebody like me." Interestingly, Pancol becomes the fifth WR to land on Denver's practice squad, joining the likes of Dane Key, Cameron Ross, Kolbe Katsis, and Michael Bandy. None of these incumbents have been promoted to the active roster in recent weeks. Speaking of the 53, the Broncos could be a little shorthanded at the position in Week 8 with Pat Bryant still on short-term injured reserve and Jaylen Waddle emerging from Sunday's win over the Cardinals with an apparent chest issue. Head coach Sean Payton indicated Monday that Marvin Mims might see an uptick in usage going forward, as he's seemingly leapfrogged Troy Franklin on the depth chart. home.headline: Broncos have 8 players on injured reserve going into Week 8
home.blurb: Five of those players — wide receiver Pat Bryant ( ankle ), offensive tackle Frank Crum , tight end Caleb Lohner , running back Tyler Badie ( thumb ) and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) — are on short-term injured reserve, which means they are eligible to return after four games (although Lohner is expected to be out until at least mid-season ). Bryant will be eligible to return in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers . Badie and Elliss, who just landed on IR over the weekend, will be eligible to return in Week 12. Another player, offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo , is on the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. He is also eligible to return after four games, but hasn't returned to practice yet. NFL clubs are allowed to designate up to eight players to return from IR each season. Denver has used three of those designations so far this season on Crum, Lohner and running back Jonah Coleman. The rookie running back was activated to the 53-man roster last week, but Crum and Lohner have not yet started their 21-day practice windows. home.blurb: When he rolled over, Waddle grabbed his left chest and shoulder area with his right hand and didn't get up until trainers came out to check on him. The team ultimately called it a chest injury. Waddle was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday with what was listed as a chest injury, then was a full participant Friday and was cleared to play against the Cardinals. Allen finished a play on Arizona's final drive, then grabbed his right hamstring and sat down. Trainers came out to look at him and he eventually walked off gingerly on his own. That development wasn't a huge surprise after Surtain was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report. Since he was first injured against San Francisco in early October, the Broncos have been aiming for a Week 8 return for Surtain. That's next weekend against Kansas City. Denver second-year defensive lineman Sai'Vion Jones has carved out a nice role for himself as a sophomore in the NFL. Jones, a 2025 third-round pick out of LSU, sacked Arizona's Jacoby Brissett early in the fourth quarter. It helped the Broncos defense get to its feet, too, after a 27-yard completion to star tight end Trey McBride (10 catches, 111 yards, TD). Denver followed up Jones' sack by forcing a turnover on downs. Five minutes into his postgame news conference after a 30-16 win over Arizona , the Broncos head coach called his own number — and criticized himself in the process. “Why hasn't anyone asked me about the dumb reverse call?” Payton wondered, getting more animated as he talked. “I'm going to answer. Everyone ask the question. “It was awful, alright, I'm sorry.” Payton had a historical comparison, too. “If you look it up, in 2008 in a similar situation, even a more radical reverse,” he said. “Fumbled. Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play.” Arizona didn't come back and beat the Broncos, of course, but the play did lose 11 yards. Denver retained possession because top wide receiver Jaylen Waddle fell on the ball. The problem this time around? Waddle also got hurt on the play . It came with 4:51 left in regulation and Denver leading by two touchdowns. Payton, who felt he and the offensive staff had put together a terrific game plan against Arizona's zone-blitzing defense, dialed up a reverse for his top receiver. The ball got fumbled, though, and Waddle jumped on it. After stopping in the medical tent for evaluation, Waddle left the game and headed back to the locker room. away.headline: A.J. Brown's Ankle Injury Should Alter New England Patriots' Expectations
away.blurb: The New England Patriots need more from wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle), but Locked On Patriots host Nick Cattles argued that his modest start should not trigger panic after a compressed return from injury. The host said Brown got consistently open against the Jets and still created a few missed opportunities against the Bears, where quarterback Drake Maye either faced pressure or went elsewhere with the ball. Cattles’ argument was not that Brown has played well in every respect, but that an early return from an ankle injury changed what reasonable expectations should be for his first season in New England. Brown’s performance against the Dolphins will not settle every question about his season, but it gives the Patriots a more useful evaluation point than a two-game stretch played on a short week after his return. Cattles framed Sunday’s road game against the Miami Dolphins as Brown’s opportunity to show the rest from the mini-bye has mattered. New England plays at Miami on Nov. 1 after its Thursday night loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Cattles said Brown’s nine catches for 101 yards through two-and-a-half games need context. He pointed to Brown playing more than 50 snaps against the New York Jets in his first game back, then taking the field again five days later in Chicago rather than receiving the gradual workload ramp-up Cattles expected. Cattles also did not dismiss Brown’s run-game issues. He said Brown has lacked consistent blocking effort and cited one incomplete deep route against Chicago where Brown appeared to lose urgency before the ball arrived. Those plays give the Patriots a legitimate concern beyond the box score, particularly while the offense searches for reliable production from its receivers. – Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson remains central to an offense Cattles believes has asked too much of him. Cattles cited Stevenson’s forced missed tackles, pass protection and ability to create yards after contact while arguing that Corey Kiner deserves a larger role to help manage Stevenson’s workload. – Patriots cornerback Carlton Davis (neck) matters beyond one coverage assignment, Cattles said. He argued Davis’ absence has forced more zone coverage, reduced the defense’s ability to blitz behind man coverage, and increased the burden on Christian Gonzalez and Marcus Jones. away.blurb: Injury Report Analysis: Patriots rule out five players for Thursday Night Football vs. the Bears Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS The Patriots ruled out CB Carlton Davis III (neck), G Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), G Ben Brown (knee), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring) for Thursday night in Chicago. On Wednesday, the Patriots ruled out LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), RG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots are also listing RT Morgan Moses (foot), S Kevin Byard III (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder), and LB Christian Ellliss (chest) as questionable for Thursday night's game. Starting on offense, the Patriots offensive line will be shorthanded, with the Pats down multiple guards who have started games this season. Along with starting RG Mike Onwenu (ankle) and top backup Greg Van Roten (thigh), who are on injured reserve, New England is also down Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Brown (knee). In his final press conference before Thursday night's game, head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed that Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will start vs. the Bears. The Pats projected starting offensive line is LT Will Campbell, LG Walter Rouse, C Jared Wilson, RG Matt Pryor, and RT Morgan Moses (questionable) or Caleb Lomu. If Moses can't finish the game and the Patriots start Lomu at guard, the rookie would need to kick back outside. Vrabel also hinted at Lomu being prepared to be the backup center. In short, that's a lot of moving parts to plan for in-game contingencies, so the clearest path forward is to start Rouse and Pryor at guard while Lomu continues in his role as the top swing tackle. Plus, Moses is listed as questionable, and if he doesn't play on the short week, Lomu would make his first NFL start at right tackle. At the skill positions, the Patriots are down two wide receivers, Doubs and Hollins, both on injured reserve. However, the Pats will have top WR A.J. Brown, whose ankle is off the injury report. New England's available wideouts are Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III, while OC Josh McDaniels can use all his tight ends and running backs. The Patriots could elevate a fifth wide receiver from the practice squad, but that feels unlikely with limited game-day roster spots. Moving over to the defense, starting CB Carlton Davis III (neck) will need to wait at least another week before returning to the lineup. Despite practicing in a limited capacity this week, Davis won't play on Thursday night, marking the third straight game he has missed with his neck injury (four out of the last six). The Patriots held lighter walkthrough sessions during a short week to prepare for the Bears, so Davis may have participated as a ramp-up for a potential return sooner rather than later. home.headline: Miami Dolphins' Caleb Douglas makes his return count with two touchdowns against New York Jets
home.blurb: “I’ve been missing them guys, sitting on the sideline,” Douglas said. “So, I’m happy I just got out there to go out there and play with them.” “I mean, I’m out there just running, man,” he said. “I’m going to the echo of the whistle.” The two-touchdown return was a first for Douglas, who called it a great game, especially at the NFL level. It also gave him a chance to contribute to the breakthrough his teammates had been pursuing while he was sidelined. For Douglas, the return brought more than a place back in the lineup. His first NFL touchdown became a two-score performance, and the celebration he had been missing from the sideline was finally one he could help create. The Miami Dolphins had glimpses early on but an injury sidelined his talent. Wide receiver Caleb Douglas had spent three games waiting to get back on the field due to an ankle injury suffered in Week 2 against San Francisco. On his first drive back against the New York Jets, he made the wait worthwhile. Douglas capped that opening drive with his first NFL touchdown against the New York Jets, then added another score in a performance that helped his team claim its first win. He finished with two catches on three targets — and both receptions ended in the end zone. In his postgame press conference, Douglas started with something simpler than the touchdowns – being back with his teammates. The second touchdown paired preparation with instinct. Quarterback Malik Willis delivered the ball from an unusual arm angle, and Douglas turned the catch into a tackle-breaking run down the sideline. Douglas credited the game plan with putting him in position. He described the Jets bringing a corner blitz and his role as the hot receiver — the quick outlet for the quarterback against that pressure. “I was hot and made a play,” he said. Once the ball arrived, there was little time to think. Asked about the move that helped him find open grass, Douglas said he was reading the defender’s approach and reacting. “I kind of felt like I had an edge and I just took it and just kept going,” he said. Malik Washington supplied a block that helped Douglas continue upfield. Even with a flag on the field and the sideline close, Douglas said his focus stayed on finishing the run. Douglas said his approach during the losing stretch was to help keep the team calm and poised. He believed the group had the talent to win; the task was to clean up the little things and keep building. “We got a squad, bro,” he said. “We just got to clean up the little things.” Against the Jets, that belief finally came with a result. “And now look, we got us a win,” Douglas said. Asked about the locker room afterward, he kept the answer short: “Man, it felt good.”

home.headline: Patriots Get Good News on Injured $42 Million Lineman Before Dolphins Game
home.blurb: Vera-Tucker exited in the second quarter of New England's Week 6 victory over his former team, the New York Jets , on Oct. 18 and did not return. New England ruled him out for Thursday night's game against the Chicago Bears, according to ESPN , then moved him to injured reserve Oct. 22 . That designation sidelines him for Weeks 7 through 10 at minimum, with a return at least possible in Week 12 after the bye. Before the move, he had started five games and 340 offensive snaps , according to The Boston Globe . Injuries, unfortunately, have shaped his career. A torn right triceps ended his 2022 season in Week 7, according to Sportsforecaster.com , and a torn Achilles did the same in Week 5 of 2023. He started 15 games in 2024 , then tore his left triceps in practice before Week 1 of 2025, wiping out his entire season . The injury epidemic cost the unit continuity and depth. Vrabel's comments leave room for Vera-Tucker to rejoin it later this season, with Week 12 the earliest possible return. Whether his hamstring cooperates by then is the question Vrabel could not answer Monday. home.blurb: Both players were listed as limited participants, and there's absolutely no guarantee that either will be ready to go for the Week 7 game against the New York Jets. "He was a big bright spot early on," Hafley said. "Everybody was excited about him from training camp to preseason and the first couple games that he played. We were counting on him and then unfortunately he got injured. Monday he was out there, limited. Today he'll be out there and getting acclimated again. My expectations can't be too high because we've got to see him practice today. We've got to see how he feels tomorrow, kind of like Kyle. And then Friday to see what he's able to do and if he's able to go and help us out. But I am excited. I'm very excited. We've got two young players practicing that we're excited about, and we'll see what they can do today." The bottom line here is that having Douglas and Louis back will help when they're able to return, but maybe it won't happen this week, and if it does, maybe we shouldn't expect too much too soon from either of them. Douglas hasn't played since Week 2, while Louis has been out since sustaining a knee injury in the opener against the Las Vegas Raiders. Also back at practice Wednesday was edge defender Robert Beal Jr., who missed the past three games because of a hamstring injury. He also was listed as a limited participant in practice. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who continues to deal with a quad injury, was the only player on the 53-man roster who did not practice Wednesday. Along with Beal, Douglas and Louis, long-snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring) and running back Jaylen Wright (foot) all were listed as limited participants. away.blurb: The season feels like it's on the line for the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7 now that Jalen Hurts is out for the season. The ever-forgiving NFC East could keep the Eagles afloat for a bit, but they need to score a win against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night to keep pace in a wide-open division. The official word on Barkley is expected closer to game time, but all signs are pointing towards the Pro Bowler making his official return in Week 7. The fact that this is a Monday night game without a clear call makes life quite difficult for managers with Barkley on their roster. The upside that Barkley offers is enormous, but if he is ruled out prior to the game there are few legitimate alternatives to plug in for him. The good news for Barkley backers is that the Eagles will likely give him everything he can handle if he's active. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out for this game, leaving Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon as the top receiving weapons for backup QB Tanner McKee. home.headline: Commanders wideout McLaurin out for the season with knee injury
home.blurb: The 31-year-old veteran is in his eighth NFL season, all with Washington, which selected him in the third round of the 2019 draft out of Ohio State. In 112 NFL games (all starts), McLaurin has 513 receptions for 7,191 yards and 42 touchdowns. The Commanders (1-4-1) have a bye week before they return to action with another prime-time game on Nov. 1 against the visiting Philadelphia Eagles (2-4). McLaurin was carted off the field late in the first quarter of the Commanders’ 23-17 loss against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night in Santa Clara, Calif. He was running a pass route to the sideline, covered by cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, when he went down under minimal contact and grabbed at his knee. He was eventually fitted with an air cast and driven off the field. An MRI in Washington on Tuesday confirmed the team’s fears of the severity of the injury. “Man, he brings a lot on and off the field,” Quinn said. “It’s a big hit and we’ll lean on a number of guys.” McLaurin ended the night with one catch for 27 yards, which helped set up a field goal. In five games this season (all starts), the team captain has 15 receptions on 27 targets for one touchdown and a team-leading 230 yards. He didn’t play in the Commanders’ Oct. 4 loss against the Indianapolis Colts in London due to a hamstring injury, but he was back the following week to make four catches for 62 yards in a tie against the visiting New York Giants. The two-time Pro Bowl selection is in the first year of a three-year, $96 million contract after signing an extension before the 2025 season. According to reports, the remaining two years have salary-cap hits of $34 million and $39.5 million, with no fully guaranteed future salary. The team could release him after this season or restructure the contract, with Washington saving about $8.5 million against the cap next year if he is released, ESPN reported. On April 1, $5.35 million of McLaurin’s salary in 2027 becomes fully guaranteed, according to Spotrac. Saquon Barkley returned Monday after missing a couple of games with a hamstring injury and had seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown despite dealing with a back issue that limited his time on the field. home.headline: Dan Quinn Drops How Commanders Will Replace Terry McLaurin
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders regrouped over their bye week and will begin trying to climb out of their early season hole against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 8. One of the biggest questions surrounding the team is how the offense will replace veteran receiver Terry McLaurin . The Commanders aren't out of the race in the NFC East. So winning remains the team's main goal. But even in the rather weak division, they sit in last place and two and a half games out of first. Dan Quinn Drops How Commanders Will Replace Terry McLaurin Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. A lot of pundits have suggested Washington could acquire a new receiver through a trade. The Commanders have two weeks to pursue that option before the league's trade deadline. But on Tuesday, Commanders head coach indicated the offense will initially lean on more from rookie wideout Antonio Williams . "Antonio is one that you'll see getting more targets to go. We'll look through the week," Quinn told reporters . "The natural progression is probably Antonio some more. "Not necessarily the same spot but a higher volume." The Commanders grabbed Williams at No. 71 overall in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Through six games, he has 18 catches, 205 yards and one touchdown this season. McLaurin will miss the rest of this season with a torn left patellar tendon. The veteran sustained the injury during Week 6 against the San Francisco 49ers on October 19. Rookie Antonio Williams to Get More Opportunities for Commanders Quinn mentioned Williams set to get more opportunities in Washington's offense while answering a question on WR1 Stefon Diggs . The Commanders head coach said Diggs's workload wouldn't change despite McLaurin set to miss the rest of the 2026 campaign. That makes sense for a couple different reasons. For one, Diggs is already getting a full workload as a starter. Secondly, he's not a long-term answer for the franchise. Diggs will turn 33 years old in November and only signed a 1-year deal this summer. Williams, on the other hand, could be a starting wideout for Washington going forward. It would be wise for the Commanders to learn what Williams is capable of while making his development a top priority the rest of the season. away.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
away.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. away.headline: Get your facts straight — NFL fans rip Dan Orlovsky for failing to grasp why Bears didn’t go all-in on DeForest Buckner trade
away.blurb: ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky, however, had questions about why the Chicago Bears didn’t do more to land Buckner. His take didn’t sit well with fans, who pushed back by pointing out that the veteran defensive tackle wanted to return to San Francisco. But fans argued that the draft compensation was only part of the equation. Reports indicated that the Bears had interest in Buckner, but the 32-year-old reportedly preferred to return to San Francisco, the team that selected him with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2016 NFL Draft. One fan directly called out Orlovsky, writing, “@danorlovsky7 are you really so dense to not realize Buckner wanted back in SF and colts honored that?” The Indianapolis Colts have shaken up their roster ahead of the NFL trade deadline, sending DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round pick. The move came shortly after Indianapolis traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks, signaling a major shift toward building for the future. NFL Fans Push Back Against Dan Orlovsky’s DeForest Buckner Take During an appearance on ESPN, Orlovsky questioned why the Bears passed up the chance to acquire an established defensive tackle for a fourth-round pick. “And then honestly, one of my big takeaways is how does Chicago not make this move? For a fourth-round pick,” Orlovsky said . At first glance, the price looked reasonable for an established interior defender. Buckner is in the final year of his contract, and his ability to pressure opposing quarterbacks could have strengthened a Chicago defensive unit that ranks 18th in PFN’s Defense Impact Score with a 74.8 grade. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Another wrote , “Percent boy is unaware Buckner preferred 49ers (former team).” A third fan added , “He wanted to be on SF. Please report this correctly.” Others were equally blunt about the situation. “Let me explain it like you’re a child. He didn’t want to come to Chicago. He wanted to go back to the team that drafted him and that was SF,” one user wrote . Another fan summed up the criticism by pointing to two key details: “2 things. 1. The bears did attempt to trade for Buckner. 2. He wanted to go to San Francisco. Get your facts straight.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor For the 6-1 49ers, bringing Buckner back would help address several injuries on their defensive line. Alfred Collins (patellar tendon) and C.J. West (knee) have been sidelined, while star edge rusher Nick Bosa has also missed time dealing with a calf injury. The veteran has recorded 31 tackles and four sacks through his first seven games of the 2026 season. Buckner also ranks fifth in PFN’s Defensive Tackle Impact Score with a 91.2 grade. San Francisco is coming off a 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. After a Week 8 bye, the 49ers will look to bounce back when they face the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. home.headline: Elijah Arroyo injury update: Seattle Seahawks receive devastating news as young tight end faces another major setback in promising NFL career
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Look, this injury hurts because Elijah Arroyo was just starting to carve out a role. The Seahawks took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft with the 50th overall pick. That’s real draft capital for a tight end. He tore his ACL in September of 2022 at Miami. That injury limited him to only nine games across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He bounced back and put together a great college career with the Hurricanes, which is a big reason Seattle used a second-round pick on him. Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo will miss the rest of the 2026 season, dealing another significant blow to his development after previous injury setbacks. How much more can Elijah Arroyo’s young career take? The Seattle Seahawks tight end is undergoing shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . Arroyo got hurt in last Thursday night’s primetime loss to the Denver Broncos as he was trying to recover a fumble by wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. It’s a brutal way to lose a season, and it’s even tougher for a second-year player who still has a lot to prove. The numbers tell the story. Arroyo will miss 11 games for Seattle, plus any potential postseason run. Seahawks fans won’t see him on the field again until 2027. Arroyo’s development takes a hit As a rookie, he played in 13 games and caught 15 passes for 179 yards and one touchdown. Those aren’t eye-popping numbers, but they’re a reasonable foundation for a first-year tight end learning the NFL game. The 2026 season hasn’t gone the way anyone hoped, though. Through six games, Arroyo had just one catch for 17 yards, obviously much less production than his rookie year. Now he won’t get the chance to turn that around. This shoulder injury is going to set him back a good bit. A second-year jump matters for young tight ends, and Arroyo loses most of that year. Losing those reps hurts. Injury history follows Arroyo from Miami to Seattle Now, Arroyo’s injury history isn’t new . It just hasn’t involved his shoulder until now. Most of his problems have been with his knee. The knee issues followed him to the NFL, though. In December 2025, Arroyo suffered a Grade One knee strain. It resulted in the Seahawks placing him on injured reserve, and him missing the rest of the season. This shoulder injury is a different animal for Elijah Arroyo. It’s the longest absence of his pro career by a wide margin. For a player who has already lost chunks of time in college and the NFL, it’s another frustrating hurdle. What it means for the Seahawks’ tight end room I’m not going to pretend this changes everything for Seattle. It’s obvious Arroyo came in to be the No. 2 tight end, even as a fairly high draft pick. The Seahawks are set at the position with AJ Barner leading the way. Seattle’s passing game will keep running through its top options, and the tight end room isn’t suddenly in crisis mode. home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks are getting closer to Zach Charbonnet's return, but head coach Mike Macdonald isn't ready to put a date on it. "He had a great week, great spirits," Macdonald said. "We have to remember, it's going to be nine months out of ACL surgery. How many people have ever done that? What's it like, Adrian Peterson?" Macdonald wasn't predicting a similar season for Charbonnet. Rather, his comments underscored the significance of attempting to return from major knee surgery on such an accelerated timeline. The roster move made him eligible to play, but Macdonald has repeatedly emphasized that his return will depend on the team's recovery plan. Charbonnet's eventual return would give Seattle another proven rushing option, particularly near the goal line. His absence has been especially noticeable with Kenneth Walker III now playing for the Chiefs and rookie Jadarian Price sidelined. Rookie Jadarian Price is expected to return to practice this week after missing multiple games with a chest injury. home.headline: Week 7 Injury Report: Chiefs at Seahawks
home.blurb: The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet for another game. Charbonnet, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, practiced fully this week, but has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Among those listed as questionable for the Seahawks is safety Nick Emmanwori , who was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, listed as limited due to a hip. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. For the Chiefs, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is out due to a concussion. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. Also out for Kansas City are receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring). For the Chiefs, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and linebacker Cooper Macdonald (knee) are both listed as questionable after being limited in Friday's practice.
